stories.title: Maulana caught on video molesting woman:Grabs her from behind in narrow alley; sparks outrage police action
stories.summary: In Moradabad, a woman wearing a burqa was harassed on the street. The woman was passing through a lane when a young man followed her. Suddenly, he came close and grabbed her from behind. After that, he started behaving obscenely. The woman immediately protested, after which the young man fled from the spot. The young man was wearing a cap on his head. Local people are identifying him as a Maulana. His face is visible in the CCTV footage. The incident is from the Barbalan area under Mugalpura police station jurisdiction. Now read the complete matter According to the victim, she was going for work on Wednesday afternoon. Then a person started following her. After following for some distance, he caught hold of her and molested the female. When she protested, the accused fled from the spot. After the incident, there was panic in the area and people are angry. Local people are identifying the youth as a Maulana. On the victim's complaint, the police have registered a case. Local people say that such incidents raise questions on the security arrangements of the area. Face visible in CCTV footage Taking cognizance of the matter, SP City Kumar Ranvijay Singh said that the accused has been identified based on CCTV footage. Police teams have been deployed for his arrest. Continuous raids are being conducted. Police say that the accused will be arrested soon and strict legal action will be taken against him. Other necessary legal procedures are also underway. The Superintendent of Police City has issued instructions to increase patrolling in the area.

stories.title: ‘Sorry Jiya, mum must die’:Bijnor woman alleges blackmail by man; says, 'I am exhausted ends life'
stories.summary: In Bijnor, a woman committed suicide after being frightened by threats from digital fraudsters. Two days after the suicide, a note was found in the woman's room on Wednesday night. In it, she mentioned being harassed by a person. The woman wrote, “Sorry Jiya, mother has to die. That boy has troubled your mother a lot. He has been blackmailing for many days. Now I am tired and committing suicide.” The woman had taken her life on Monday night by hanging from a fan in her room. The family members had also performed the last rites without informing the police. However, the family became suspicious after continuous video calls on the woman's mobile. A suicide note was found during the search of the room. After this, the family members told the police everything and filed an FIR. The case is from the city Kotwali area. Now know the complete case Monica Singh (30), a housewife, was a resident of village Faridpur Bhogi. Her husband Randhir Singh (33) works in a factory. They have two daughters - Jiya (8) and Nandini (11). Nandini told, “On Monday night, mother was writing something on paper.” When I asked what happened, Mamma, she said, “Nothing, dear. Just writing something. After writing, mother put both of us sisters to sleep. When we woke up on Tuesday morning, we saw mother hanging from the fan with the support of a dupatta.” Seeing the mother's condition, both daughters started crying and screaming. Family members also came running. Monica's maternal family also arrived upon receiving the information. The family could not understand any reason for the suicide. Fearing social stigma, the family performed the last rites without informing the police. Suspicion deepened due to video call on mobile Monica's nephew Sanyog said - After the last rites, everyone was at home. Aunt's phone was ringing continuously. When the phone was answered, a person appeared in police uniform on video call. He identified himself as being from the Crime Branch. He said to let him talk to Monica. After the conversation, we became suspicious of cyber crime. Suicide note found during search of room The nephew said - After this, we searched aunt's room. Then a suicide note was found in a diary. It mentioned being harassed and blackmailed by a boy. After this, when aunt's mobile was checked, calls, messages and audio recordings from 5 different numbers were found on WhatsApp. In this, someone was claiming to be a Crime Branch officer, while someone was trying to scare her by making serious allegations like smuggling against her aunt. The fraudsters kept her under 'digital arrest'. They demanded money and threatened to ruin her life. After the suicide note was found, family members approached the police and filed a complaint. Read what was written in the suicide note Sorry my dear husband, I love you I have many things to tell you. I have a lot to share with you. A boy has been troubling me a lot for many days. Now he is blackmailing me. Please, if possible, forgive me. I love you very much, so I cannot lie to you. Please, after my death, take care of my children. If I get another life, may I get you again. Thank you for coming into my life. Our wedding anniversary is coming. Sorry, for not being able to stay with you. Please show this letter to my family members. Sorry to my mom-dad, brother-sister-in-law, everyone. You all have been with me a lot in my life. Sister-in-law, take care of my mom. May I get you as my mom, dad, brother and sister-in-law in every birth. Sorry Jiya, mom has to die. That boy has troubled your mom a lot. Family was also being threatened Even after Monica's death, the threats from cyber fraudsters have not stopped. Several calls came on Wednesday too. They were pressuring the family members to let them talk to Monica. The family members said that on not letting them talk to Monica, threats were being made to send husband Randhir to jail and harm the entire family. Husband gave three mobile numbers to police Monica's husband Ranveer has filed an FIR at the city police station. He has also provided the police with 3 mobile numbers from which Monica's phone was receiving continuous calls. It was reported that a young man had made a video call even during the last rites. SP Abhishek Jha said that the police were not informed about the woman's suicide. The family members had performed the last rites. Later, information was received about finding a suicide note. It mentions being harassed by a young man. The family members have also expressed suspicion of cybercrime. Currently, a case has been registered based on the complaint and investigation is underway.

stories.title: Non-bailable warrant issued against Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar:Threatened to throw shoes at BJP leaders in 2019
stories.summary: The MP-MLA court in Mau has issued a non-bailable warrant against Cabinet Minister Omprakash Rajbhar. OP Rajbhar was not appearing in court in a case of threatening BJP leaders. The court took a strict stance on this. The next hearing of the case has been scheduled for May 16. This matter dates back to the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. There was a Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party rally in Ratanpura Bazaar. It is alleged that Rajbhar told his workers and the public at the rally, "If BJP people come asking for votes, beat them with shoes. An FIR was registered at Haldharpur police station in this case. After this, dates for appearance came several times but the minister was not appearing for the hearing. Therefore, the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate (MP-MLA) Dr. Krishna Pratap Singh issued this order on Wednesday. Know entire case According to the prosecution, during the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, a public meeting was organized at Ratanpura market. In this meeting, Omprakash Rajbhar used indecent language against leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party. Not only this, he is also accused of saying from the stage that if BJP people come asking for votes, they should be beaten with shoes. This falls under the category of violation of the code of conduct. Hearing was ongoing in court In this case, hearings have been ongoing in court for quite some time. The case is pending in the MP-MLA Court, where matters related to public representatives are heard. The court had summoned OP Rajbhar to appear several times, but he continuously failed to appear in court. Due to this reason, the court took the matter seriously and adopted a strict stance. Absence proved costly Despite repeated summons and directives, when he failed to appear in court, the court considered it as contempt and decided to issue a non-bailable warrant. This step by the court indicates that no leniency will be shown in this matter anymore and the accused will have to appear before the court at any cost. What is a non-bailable warrant? A Non-Bailable Warrant (NBW) is a serious legal process in which the police are directed to arrest the accused and present them directly in court. In this situation, the accused is not guaranteed immediate bail, and further proceedings are determined only after appearing before the court.

stories.title: Monkey on runway halts IndiGo flight:Pilot applies emergency brakes during Lucknow–Raipur take-off
stories.summary: On Thursday morning at Lucknow Airport, a monkey suddenly appeared on the runway in front of an IndiGo flight. The pilot applied emergency brakes, which caused panic among the 135 passengers on board. The aircraft was brought back to the taxiway. It could be dispatched to Raipur after a delay of about an hour and fifteen minutes. According to airport sources, this incident occurred at 8:55 AM with IndiGo Airlines flight (6E 6521) going to Raipur. The aircraft had covered some distance on the runway for takeoff. Just then, a monkey suddenly appeared in front of the aircraft, forcing the pilot to immediately apply emergency brakes. After the aircraft stopped, it was brought back to the taxiway Due to the sudden braking, all passengers and crew members on board the aircraft panicked. After this, the aircraft was brought back from the runway to the taxiway. As soon as the airport administration received the information, there was a commotion. The 'Follow Me' vehicle personnel deployed in airport security immediately took action and chased the monkey away from the runway. After about an hour and a quarter, the aircraft was dispatched again for Raipur. The Civil Aviation Department has ordered an investigation into this incident. The monkey kept jumping around for about an hour The monkey kept jumping around the runway and its surroundings for about an hour. After considerable difficulty, the runway security staff managed to chase it away. The monkey ran off towards the airport boundary wall in the direction of Rahimabad village.

stories.title: Loan-funded dream home turns to ashes:Massive blaze in 15-storey society engulfs multiple floors; 10 flats destroyed
stories.summary: A devastating fire broke out on Wednesday morning in a 15-storey apartment building, Gaur Green Avenue Society in Ghaziabad, leaving several families homeless as their flats were completely gutted. The fire started on the 9th floor and rapidly spread to nearly seven floors. Residents rushed to save their lives, with many fleeing through staircases as lifts were shut. Some tried to retrieve belongings, while elderly and ailing residents were left trapped inside. Firefighters managed to rescue at least 10 people, including a sick elderly man, from the blaze. After nearly three hours of effort, the fire was brought under control. Around 10 flats were completely destroyed. “We lost everything,” residents say “We have lost everything. We bought this flat with our lifetime savings and a loan. Not even a spoon is left,” said Kayra Sharma, breaking down after her flat was destroyed. She added, “We always switched off the electricity before leaving home—even the fridge was never left on. We don’t know what suddenly went wrong.” Kayra was seen crying inconsolably on a video call with her husband, as women around her tried to comfort her, saying it was fortunate that lives were saved. Panic during evacuation Recounting the incident, Kayra said everything was normal until she heard loud noises. “When I stepped out, I saw the flat below ours on fire. People told me to run. The lifts were shut, and there was fire everywhere—from bottom to top,” she said. “I folded my hands and prayed that something might be saved, but when the fire was extinguished, everything inside was gone.” Woman cries holding child as family loses home In another flat, Pushpa Verma, wife of engineer Anshuman Verma, was seen sobbing while holding her young child. Speaking to her family over the phone, she said, “Everything has been destroyed. Nothing is left. Only our lives have been saved.” The affected families have been temporarily shifted to the society’s community hall. Fire spreads rapidly across residential block Resident Monika Setia said the fire spread quickly across the block, which houses about 100 flats, while the entire society has around 450 families. “We heard shouting and ran out. People were rushing down the stairs. A guard informed us that firefighters had been called, but by the time they arrived, the fire had already spread,” she said. Elderly rescued, flats broken open Residents said an 85-year-old woman, Ramwati Devi, was rescued with difficulty. Several locked flats had to be broken open using rescue cutters to control the fire and check for trapped occupants. At least seven locked flats were forced open during the operation. A sick elderly man was also rescued and taken to hospital. Major firefighting operation Chief Fire Officer Rahul Pal said two teams were deployed to evacuate residents through staircases. Among those rescued was Mohammad Ayub, an elderly man on oxygen support. A total of 18 fire tenders and two hydraulic platforms from Ghaziabad and Noida were deployed. Around 74 firefighters worked to bring the blaze under control. Cause of Fire Under Investigation Additional Police Commissioner (Law and Order) Raj Karan Nair said, The fire started on the 9th floor and spread upwards. All residents were evacuated safely in time. Around two dozen nearby flats were saved. The cause of the fire is being investigated.

stories.title: DCM Pathak alleges Samajwadi Party attempted to kill Mayawati:CM Yogi slams opposition over women’s issues during UP Assembly session
stories.summary: A stormy special session of the Uttar Pradesh legislature witnessed sharp political attacks on Thursday, with Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath targeting the Samajwadi Party (SP), Congress, and the INDIA bloc over women’s issues and past incidents. Deputy CM appeals for women’s representation As proceedings began at 11 am in both Houses, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak folded his hands before the opposition and appealed for greater representation of women in Parliament. “I request with folded hands and bowed head—please ensure our daughters and sisters reach the country’s highest decision-making body,” he said. Allegation over Mayawati 'guest house incident’ Referring to the infamous guest house incident, Pathak alleged that Samajwadi Party “goons and mafia” had attempted to kill BSP leader Mayawati, and that she survived due to the BJP’s intervention. CM Yogi slams opposition, Cites Shah Bano Case Earlier, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused Samajwadi Party, Congress, and the INDIA bloc of being “anti-women,” citing their conduct in Parliament on April 16 and 17. He said Congress’ decline began over its handling of the Shah Bano case, alleging that the party bowed to pressure from clerics instead of ensuring justice. “If Congress had not succumbed to pressure and had ensured justice for Shah Bano, it would not have faced such decline,” he said. Resolution over Women’s Reservation Bill The Chief Minister also introduced a condemnation proposal over the alleged blocking of the Women’s Reservation Bill in Parliament, aiming to project Congress and Samajwadi Party as anti-women. However, the opposition is expected to counter this claim, stating that the Women’s Reservation Bill was already passed in 2023 and accusing the government of delaying its implementation. Uproar and Protests inside assembly The Assembly witnessed noisy scenes as BJP and SP legislators raised slogans against each other. BJP women MLAs arrived holding placards reading “Sadda Haq Ithe Rakh” (Give us our rights here), while SP legislators demanded implementation of the Women’s Reservation Act passed in 2023. Samajwadi Party members also surrounded Assembly Speaker Satish Mahana and Deputy CM Keshav Maurya during the protest. Political tensions escalate The developments highlight intensifying political tensions in Uttar Pradesh, with both sides using women’s representation and past controversies as key points of attack.

stories.title: Under-construction hospital building collapses in Lucknow:Two labourers pulled from debris; one declared dead
stories.summary: An under-construction building collapsed near an NTPC facility, leaving one worker dead and another injured in Lucknow’s Vibhutikhand area on Thursday morning According to officials, the incident took place around 10 am during excavation work for a basement. Soil from behind a wall suddenly caved in, trapping two labourers under the debris. Police and fire brigade teams rushed to the spot immediately after receiving the alert and launched a rescue operation. One of the workers was pulled out in an unconscious state and rushed to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The deceased has been identified as 35-year-old Laxmi Shankar Awasthi, a resident of Ramnagar in Barabanki district. The second worker, Tulsi Ram from Bhikampatti village, sustained minor injuries. He was taken to Lohia Institute for treatment and later discharged after receiving primary care. Hospital construction underway, map approved Officials from the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) inspected the site following the incident. Additional Secretary C.P. Tripathi confirmed that the building plan for plot D63 had been approved and that a hospital was being constructed on the site. Further investigation is being carried out by the police. See pictures- Authorities cite soil collapse as cause Vibhutikhand Inspector Amar Singh stated that police received information about the soil collapse around 10 am. Local police, along with fire brigade and SDRF teams, reached the location promptly and conducted rescue operations on a war footing. Both trapped workers were successfully pulled out from the debris, but one could not be saved. Authorities are continuing to probe the circumstances surrounding the incident.

stories.title: Body found buried in soil in Gorakhpur:Locals panic after spotting human hand sticking out
stories.summary: A body buried in mud was discovered in Gorakhpur after a human hand was seen protruding from the soil in a dry drain on Thursday morning. The shocking sight triggered panic among local residents, who immediately raised an alarm. Incident reported from Gulariha area The incident took place in Jainpur Gram Sabha, Tola Masoodabad, under the Gulariha area. Early in the morning, people who had come out for a walk noticed a human hand sticking out from the soil in the dried Chorahiya drain. Initially startled, they began shouting, drawing a crowd of more than 50 people. See pictures from the crime scene Police begin recovery efforts On receiving information, police reached the spot and began efforts to recover the body. Laborers have been called in to remove the mud, after which the identity of the deceased will be ascertained. Animal activity suspected Strands of hair were also found scattered at the scene. Locals suspect that animals may have pulled out the hair while scavenging. Authorities are investigating the case, and further details are expected once the body is fully recovered.

stories.title: UP’s Banda hotter than the world’s scorching deserts:America's Death Valley once touched 57°C; where do temperatures stand now?
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh’s Banda has been making headlines across India and beyond in recent days — for its scorching heat. On 27 April, the city’s temperature touched 47.6°C, making it the hottest city in the world that day. This raised a striking question: Is Banda now hotter than some of the world’s fiercest deserts? If yes, how hot are those places? Meteorologists say Banda’s temperature has been rising steadily over the past two decades. In June 2019, the mercury here had crossed 49°C. According to weather website AccuWeather, on 27 April 2026, temperature in the Thar Desert in Rajasthan was 46°C, while Africa’s Sahara Desert recorded 30°C. What about the world’s hottest places — Death Valley, Lut Desert and Dallol? Some of the hottest places on Earth include Death Valley, Lut Desert and Dallol. Temperatures there are measured in different ways. Based on air temperature: According to the World Meteorological Organization, Death Valley in the US is considered the hottest place on Earth. On 10 July 1913, air temperature there reached 56.7°C. However, on 27 April 2026, it was 28°C. Based on land surface temperature: Iran’s Lut Desert is considered the hottest place in the world in terms of ground temperature. Satellite readings by NASA recorded land temperatures of 70.7°C there between 2003 and 2009. Some parts are so hot that life is nearly impossible. On 27 April, air temperature there was 27°C. Based on average annual temperature: Dallol in Ethiopia remains hot throughout the year, with an average temperature of around 34–35°C. On 27 April, it recorded 35°C. Why is it so hot in Banda... Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh of the Regional Meteorological Centre in Lucknow says Banda’s terrain is a mix of rugged plateau and plains. Its land contains granite and rocks from the Vindhya range. Stone and rock heat up quickly under the sun but cool slowly, meaning extreme heat lingers in the atmosphere even after sunset. Meteorologist Dr Dinesh Shah of Banda University of Agriculture and Technology says hot winds blowing in from Rajasthan are pushing temperatures higher. Intense sunlight and low humidity are making the heat feel even harsher. How is temperature measured? Atul Kumar Singh explains that temperature is measured using a mercury thermometer placed inside a wooden box designed to allow air to flow through it. The instrument is left in the area for 24 hours, recording temperature continuously. It stops at the highest point reached, which meteorologists later record. Dr Dinesh Shah says three departments monitor temperature in Banda. The Meteorological Department records readings near the Collectorate. UP Disaster Management has installed digital automatic sensors in every tehsil. The agriculture university measures temperature through both automatic sensors and mercury thermometers. Its campus is 5–6 km outside the city, so its readings are considered representative of rural areas. Are nearby cities equally hot? Districts around Banda are also facing severe heat, though temperatures remain slightly lower. On 27 April, when Banda recorded 47.6°C, neighbouring districts including Fatehpur, Hamirpur, Mahoba and Chitrakoot were hovering close to 46°C. According to the weather department, temperatures in these areas are likely to rise gradually in the coming days. Across Bundelkhand — including Banda, Jhansi, Lalitpur, Jalaun, Hamirpur, Mahoba and Chitrakoot — the heat pattern is expected to remain similar, with temperatures ranging between 44°C and 46°C. Heatwave impact now visible in hospitals The intense heat is beginning to affect public health. Chief Medical Superintendent K. Kumar at Banda District Hospital said 500–600 patients are arriving daily, and on some days the number crosses 1,000. Hundreds require admission. Most are suffering from vomiting, diarrhoea and stomach pain. Last year, in 2024, around 200 bats died due to extreme heat, and several parrots also died. This was confirmed by Chief Veterinary Officer Nirmal Kumar. To help people cope, Banda Municipal Council has set up cooling centres, while children are frequently seen bathing in the Ken River to escape the heat.

stories.title: UP storm havoc leaves 14 dead:IMD issues alert for 68 cities; rain lashes 5 districts including Kanpur and Mathura
stories.summary: Weather conditions across Uttar Pradesh have changed dramatically, with storms and rainfall interrupting the ongoing heatwave and scorching temperatures. Cloud cover has spread across the state, with intermittent sunshine. Early Thursday morning, heavy rain accompanied by thunder and lightning lashed cities including Kanpur, Agra, Mathura, and Unnao. Lucknow witnessed intermittent drizzle along with cool winds. Alert in 68 districts, lightning risk high According to the Meteorological Department, rain alerts have been issued for 68 districts in Uttar Pradesh on Thursday. Lightning strikes and strong winds are also likely. The weather is expected to remain unstable for the next five days. On Wednesday, more than 30 districts, including Prayagraj and Varanasi, experienced storms and rainfall. Hailstorms were reported in at least 10 districts, including Lucknow, Barabanki, Unnao, Amethi, Rae Bareli, and Jaunpur. 14 dead, several injured amid storm havoc The severe storms caused widespread damage, uprooting trees and electricity poles and collapsing several mud houses across the state. A total of 14 people lost their lives due to storm-related incidents: At least 21 people were injured in various incidents. Wind speeds reached 100 km/h in Varanasi and 87 km/h in Ayodhya during the storm. Banda remains hottest despite rainfall Despite the change in weather, Banda remained the hottest city in the state, recording a maximum temperature of 45.8°C. Rainfall data shows: Weather system behind the change Atul Kumar Singh, senior scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre in Lucknow, said the change in weather is due to a cyclonic system formed over northern Pakistan and nearby Jammu Kashmir. He added that rainfall activity is likely to continue into the first week of May, providing relief from heat but also bringing thunderstorms, lightning, and possible hail. Five-day weather forecast

stories.title: 46 days since 'Opportunistic Pandit' controversy, investigation team 'missing':BJP MLAs, leaders who wrote letters to Yogi ordered to stay quiet
stories.summary: On March 14, 2026, a question was asked in the UP Police SI recruitment exam: 'Select one word for the phrase that changes according to opportunity'. The Brahmin community was enraged. Brahmin MLAs and leaders wrote angry letters to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak immediately ordered an investigation. The CM also said that those who make such questions should be found and blacklisted. 46 days have passed. MLAs have not received replies to their letters. It is not even known whether an investigation team has been formed or not. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to three BJP MLAs who registered protests, one senior leader, one SP MLA and officials of the UP Police Recruitment Board. BJP leaders and MLAs spoke on the condition of anonymity because they have received a message from the high command to remain silent. Read their answers... 1. BJP state-level leader in UP Question: You had written a letter to the CM, did you follow up on it? Answer: Yes, I inquired. Got a vague response. We have been told that the board's team is investigating this matter. Who all are in the team, we were not told. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak had ordered the investigation. You can ask him. Question: Can you write another letter to know the status of the investigation? Answer: Yes, we can do that. We will do it too. Question: The board is in Lucknow itself, don't you have access to the officials? Answer: We have access to everyone, but the officials are helpless as they have to work on orders from people above. Why would they tell us anything formally. We have found out informally that the investigation team was not formed at all. A verbal response was given. Nothing happened in writing. 2. BJP MLA 1 Question: When will the investigation report come, have you taken any follow-up? Answer: Yes, a letter was written. The Chief Minister had assured that there will be an investigation. Who all are in the team, that is a confidential matter. The investigation is going on secretly. We cannot tell you. The matter is serious. The report will take time to come. We will take follow-up again. We will inquire about the status and inform you. We had written the letter to express our displeasure. The displeasure has been registered. Now the investigation is the government's matter. 3. BJP MLA 2 Question: How far has the opportunistic Pandit case progressed? Answer: It has now been resolved. The Board has given an oral response that the matter was incorrectly publicized. Pandit was given as an option in the paper. It was not stated that Pandit was the correct option. If someone had ticked Pandit, it would have been the wrong answer. Options are always meant to confuse students. This option was also meant to confuse students. Neither the Board nor the paper setter had any mischievous or conspiratorial intent. Nevertheless, it is necessary to identify mischievous elements who have a habit of targeting leaders of a particular caste. This issue should be viewed not as a single incident but by connecting several events. Question: Why aren't you people creating pressure for an investigation? Answer: The party has sent a message to the MLAs who wrote the letter to maintain peace. There is no need to write or ask anything more. In politics, messaging happens, not through writing or any legal way. Just a message is received. And people understand. 4. BJP MLA 3 Question: How far has the investigation into the opportunistic Pandit case reached? Answer: We have been told by the CM office that the investigation is ongoing. We are also waiting. Now we will send a reminder. When we go to Lucknow, we will find out the status. Whether the investigation team has people from within the board or also from the government, we have not been told. 5. Amitabh Bajpai, SP MLA Question: You had sent a complaint letter to the CM, did you get a response? Answer: Do you think anyone gets a response from there! They don't listen to their own MLAs, why would they listen to us. I have written letters to them on several issues. Till date, I haven't received a response to any. There's no benefit of filing RTI either. Those also get stuck. When we inquired, we were told a team is investigating. Who all are in the team, which board officials are under the scope of investigation, nobody has any information about this. You should also check with BJP MLAs. They are insiders, perhaps they might have some information. 6. Sources from UP Police Recruitment and Promotion Board Question: Has an investigation team been formed, who all were in the team that set the paper? Answer: To our knowledge, no such team has been formed. A meeting has definitely taken place at the board. The Director had instructed all board officials not to talk to anyone about this matter. Even then, it was not described as anyone's conspiracy or mischief, but was said to be a controversy arising from a misunderstanding. The team that set the paper was from outside. It was found out that it was some firm from Karnataka. The company's owner is high profile. I'm not 100% sure about the name. The company had connections with Karnataka and Maharashtra as well. The owner is from UP. He is from a very sensitive zone, that's why I'm not taking the name right now. Called the Board Chairman several times, told repeatedly he was ‘busy in meetings’ We called UP Police Recruitment Board Chairman S. B. Shirodkar several times. Every time the phone was answered at the office number. Citing the sir's busy schedule and meetings, we were asked to call back after some time. When we called back after some time, we received the same response. We also called his mobile number several times, but could not speak to him. We spoke twice with the Chairman's PA Ashok Verma. The first time he advised speaking on the CUG number and office number. When we couldn't get through, he said, when I go to the office, I will arrange for you to speak. The next time we spoke, the response came with irritation. I am on leave. Don't call me repeatedly. 52 Brahmin MLAs in UP, 41 from BJP There are a total of 52 Brahmin MLAs in the UP Legislative Assembly. Of these, 41 are from BJP, 4 from Nishad Party which is in alliance with BJP, 1 from Apna Dal (S), 5 from opposition Samajwadi Party and 1 from Congress belong to the Brahmin community. According to CSDS-Lokniti's estimated data, the Brahmin population in UP is considered to be between 9% to 11%. OBC 45% to 50%, Scheduled Caste 21% to 22%, Scheduled Caste 19% to 20%, Rajput 7% to 8%, Vaishya 3% to 4% and Others 2% to 3%.

stories.title: Become Amitabh Bachchan’s neighbour for ₹7 crore:Is Big B an Ayodhya resident or just an investor? Truth behind his 3 properties
stories.summary: “Saryu Ghat in Ayodhya has become a unique confluence of faith and progress… Crores of people are now arriving here from every corner of the world… Welcome to this golden era of Ayodhya, of which I too am a resident…” In a video, Amitabh Bachchan is seen calling himself a resident of Ayodhya. Last month, reports emerged that Amitabh had bought a third property in Ayodhya. Meanwhile, land prices around the plots linked to him have surged sharply. Buyers are even being charged a ₹10 lakh premium for the chance to become Amitabh Bachchan’s ‘neighbour’. Projecting Amitabh Bachchan as a resident of Ayodhya and selling nearby plots at premium rates is part of a strategy jointly built around a real estate company and Amitabh Bachchan’s company. Amitabh recorded promotional videos branding the real estate project. Instead of paying him in cash, the company allotted him plots in its township — a model described as a ‘barter system’. That, in itself, may be standard business practice. But the company then appears to have adopted a smart sales tactic. By projecting Amitabh as an Ayodhya resident, it began charging premium rates on plots surrounding his property. To verify the truth behind Amitabh Bachchan’s Ayodhya property and the claims of making buyers his ‘neighbours’, a Dainik Bhaskar team carried out an on-ground investigation. Here is the full reveal. Ground visit to ‘The Saryu Project’ Travelling 130 km from Lucknow, the team reached Ayodhya. Around 7 km from the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple site, on the Azamgarh bypass, lies The Saryu Project township. Three properties linked to Amitabh Bachchan are located here. Construction work was underway at parts of the site when the team arrived. Large hoardings featuring Amitabh Bachchan are placed throughout the project, with the actor lending his credibility to the development. When the team asked to see Amitabh’s plot, security at the gate denied entry. The guard directed them to the company office at Saadatganj crossing for details. The team then travelled 17 km to Saadatganj, where a man named Kalam, associated with the company, met them after the guard said no sales staff were present. Kalam seated the team in a meeting hall and explained the project. Since premium buyers were understood to be the target market, the team posed as representatives of a retired UP officer looking to invest. Kalam then laid out the complete pricing strategy for plots. Reporter: Can we get a plot next to Amitabh Bachchan’s? Kalam: But plots in our company project are very expensive. Reporter: How expensive? Kalam: ₹16,000 per sq ft. Reporter: Is it expensive because of Amitabh Bachchan? Kalam: Yes… because of Amitabh Bachchan, and because of our company too. Calling someone on the phone, Kalam asked whether any plot was vacant next to the one Amitabh Bachchan had bought, saying a client was sitting in front of him and asking for the layout and plot size. “Amitabh Bachchan will come here in his final years” Kalam: The The Leela hotel is coming up on 5 acres, and Amitabh Bachchan’s land is right next to it. Reporter: Amitabh Bachchan has three properties there, right? Kalam: Two properties have been registered. Reporter: But where will Amitabh Bachchan settle here? Kalam: He will come. He will come for Ayodhya darshan. In his final years, he will come here. At that moment, Kalam received a call. After speaking, he turned back and said a 5,000 sq ft plot was available next to Amitabh’s property for ₹7.25 crore, at ₹14,300 per sq ft. Reporter: Look, a deal can happen, but do you actually know whether Amitabh Bachchan will come here or not? Kalam: I told you, he will come — in his later years. Reporter: Till then, you will keep selling on Amitabh Bachchan’s name. Kalam: Yes, he is a brand. Branding is happening. If you don’t want a company plot, we can get you one nearby. Reporter: At what rate? Kalam: ₹2,000 per sq ft. Reporter: ₹2,000 nearby, and seven times higher in the company project? Kalam: That is because of the company — he is our brand ambassador. Reporter: But his name is also being sold, isn’t it? Kalam: Both names carry equal value. Many actors have bought land here. Kalam then pointed to adjacent farmers’ land and suggested the team inspect it. He informed the village head about the visit. The next day, the team returned and met village head Shivpujan, who showed a 16-biswa (21,600 sq ft) roadside plot. This land backs directly onto Amitabh Bachchan’s plot. Kalam quoted ₹2,000 per sq ft, while the village head quoted ₹2,500 per sq ft. Construction of The Leela hotel is also underway there on a 5-acre site. Plot deals being handled from Mumbai, not through site visits After meeting the village head, the team returned to the township gate. Security stopped them again, took their number, and asked them to wait. After an hour, they were introduced to project GM O.P. Pandey, who shared the number of Mumbai sales head Namita. The team expressed interest in buying a plot next to Amitabh’s property. Namita said someone would contact them soon. The next day, senior sales manager Sanket More from the Mumbai office called and arranged a Zoom meeting, joined by Shivam and Pragati Navalkar. Branding strategy: Amitabh gets plots for promotional videos, company uses his name to sell nearby land at premium rates Shivam: To be honest, most celebrities buy land. Amitabh Bachchan is from Prayagraj, so he has a stronger connection with Ayodhya. He has no plan to settle in Alibaug because he already has dozens of homes in Mumbai. But Ayodhya attracts him. Reporter: Did your company gift Amitabh the first plot in exchange for branding? Pragati: Yes, that is correct. Reporter: Was the gift made to Amitabh Bachchan or his father? Shivam: Amitabh made five different promotional videos for us. His hoardings are everywhere. In one way, you can understand it as a barter system. He invested ₹40 crore. But for the two 5,000 sq ft plots he took, he did branding worth ₹14–15 crore, and took those two units in return. Reporter: Which plot are you offering me? Shivam: This one above the red block marking. It is 5,000 sq ft, east-facing. It faces the bungalow Amitabh Bachchan will build. The best part is it directly faces Amitabh’s plot and is available. It is management-held inventory. Reporter: What is the price? Shivam: ₹14,400 per sq ft. Total price ₹7.20 crore. This includes stamp duty, registration and infrastructure development charges. The next day, sales head Kashish Thakkar called. After taking basic details, she later explained pricing in detail. Kashish: If you buy a plot near Amitabh Bachchan’s property, you will have to pay an additional ₹10 lakh premium charge. Anywhere else in the project remains ₹14,400 per sq ft. Reporter: So ₹10 lakh extra if the plot is near Amitabh? Kashish: Yes. How much extra is being charged in Amitabh’s name? A 5,000 sq ft plot facing Amitabh’s property inside The Saryu Project costs: ₹7.20 crore + ₹10 lakh premium = ₹7.30 crore (at ₹14,400 per sq ft). A 5,000 sq ft farmer-owned plot adjoining Amitabh’s property outside the township costs around ₹2.46 crore, including stamp duty, registration and diversion expenses (at ₹2,500 per sq ft). This means a 5,000 sq ft plot is being sold at ₹4.84 crore extra — nearly three times higher — by leveraging Amitabh Bachchan’s name and celebrity branding. When approached for comment, officials at Amitabh Bachchan’s company ABCL did not respond on their Mumbai landline number. Ayodhya land prices rise up to fourfold in 2 years The consecration ceremony of Ram Lalla at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple took place on 22 January 2024. At that time, land in the core temple area was priced at ₹614 per sq ft. It has now climbed to ₹2,524 per sq ft. A 5,000 sq ft plot that cost ₹30.70 lakh then is now worth ₹1.25 crore — a fourfold increase. Residential areas such as Rakabganj, Devkali and Awadh Vihar have seen prices rise by 200%, while rates in Tehra Manjha on Ayodhya’s outskirts have tripled. The government had not revised circle rates in Ayodhya for eight years, but rising demand after the consecration led to annual hikes. How are land prices fixed? There is no such thing as a ‘celebrity neighbour charge’ To understand plot pricing and premium charges, the team spoke to senior Lucknow High Court advocate Prashant Singh Atal, who explained pricing norms and RERA regulations. Company says all norms are being followed O.P. Pandey, GM overseeing The Saryu project in Ayodhya, said the company operates according to its own norms and conditions. Land is being bought and sold within those rules, and the project is expanding while complying with all regulations. He said properties sold to Amitabh Bachchan and others were done under the same policy. Power of attorney used for Amitabh-linked registration Company official Jagbir Singh said Rajesh Yadav completed registration for Amitabh Bachchan’s company using power of attorney. He added that he had no information on whether Amitabh acquired the land through a barter arrangement

stories.title: BJP first choice on 31 of 46 Muslim-dominated seats:UP residents want new candidates on 18 seats; SP leads on 15
stories.summary: Muslims remain a major factor in Uttar Pradesh politics, accounting for around 19% of the state’s population. There are 46 Assembly seats where the Muslim population ranges between 30% and 60%. Of these, 24 are currently held by Bharatiya Janata Party, 20 by Samajwadi Party, and one each by Apna Dal (Sonelal) and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party. According to the Dainik Bhaskar survey, people picked BJP as their first choice on 31 of these 46 Muslim-dominated seats, while SP emerged as the preferred party on the remaining 15 seats. This suggests SP could lose ground on five such seats. BJP’s allies also appear set to lose one seat each, though those seats are seen shifting towards BJP itself. On 18 of the 46 seats, voters said they would prefer new faces as candidates in the 2027 Assembly elections. 13 seats represented by Muslim MLAs Out of the 46 Muslim-dominated seats, 13 are currently represented by Muslim MLAs. Among them, 11 belong to SP, while one each is from Apna Dal (S) and SBSP. The survey found that voters do not want 10 of these 13 MLAs to be fielded again. Only three received a positive response from voters for another term. 5 seats where new faces emerged as first choice 33 Muslim-dominated seats represented by Hindu MLAs Among the remaining 33 Muslim-majority seats, BJP currently holds 24 and SP holds 9. The survey found that voters do not want 27 of these MLAs renominated. On two seats — represented by Shahjahanpur MLA and Finance Minister Suresh Khanna, and Khalilabad BJP MLA Ankur Tiwari — voters were unable to form a clear opinion. Only four sitting MLAs received strong support for another term. 13 seats where voters preferred fresh candidates Several constituencies saw clear support for new faces: 18 more seats with Muslim MLAs, but Muslim population below 30% Apart from these 46 seats, there are 18 constituencies where Muslim population is below 30%, but the MLA is Muslim. Of these, 16 are held by SP and two by Rashtriya Lok Dal. The survey found that voters were unhappy with 17 of these 18 MLAs. Only Kanth MLA Kamal Akhtar received majority support, with 52% wanting him fielded again as SP’s candidate. Among SP’s 16 seats in this category, BJP was chosen as first-choice party on eight, while SP retained the lead on the other eight. On both RLD-held seats, voters picked BJP as their first preference. New faces became the preference on 3 out of 18

stories.title: Triple murder accused birthday boy Jeetu Saini killed in encounter:Bulandshahr Police shoot him 3 times; cake smear triggered crime
stories.summary: Days after a birthday party in Bulandshahr ended in a triple murder over a dispute involving cake-smearing, police on Thursday killed the main accused, Jeetu Saini, in an encounter. Jeetu was accused of shooting dead 3 relatives of a BJP councillor at a gym in Khurja before fleeing. A reward of Rs 50,000 had been announced on him. Jeetu was hit by three bullets in the exchange of fire. Police took him to the district hospital, where he died during treatment. Heavy police deployment remains outside the hospital. Inspector Mohammad Aslam and Head Constable Mohit Malik were also injured in the encounter. Both have been admitted to a higher medical centre. Besides them, bullets also struck the bulletproof jackets of two constables, Ramphal and Kapil. On the night of 25 April, at RJS Fitness Gym, birthday boy Jeetu Saini (30) allegedly murdered the brother, cousin and nephew of a BJP councillor. Jeetu had also earlier served as a former BSP city president. Before Jeetu, police had already shot and arrested Mayank Saini, Rinku Saini and Bharat Saini in separate encounters linked to the same case. SP says accused opened fire on police, was killed in retaliatory action Bulandshahr SP Dinesh Kumar Singh said six police teams were conducting raids in search of the accused. During the operation, a police team signalled two men travelling on a scooter to stop. On seeing the police, the accused tried to flee and then opened fire at the police team. In retaliatory firing by police, one criminal was seriously injured. He was first taken to the Community Health Centre (CHC) and later referred to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police recovered a .32 bore pistol, the scooter, and a large quantity of empty shells and live cartridges from the spot. One accused managed to escape, and police are continuously carrying out raids to trace him. Jeetu’s video reel: “I will definitely kill… make arrangements to save yourself” Earlier, a video reel of accused Jeetu Saini had surfaced. In it, he is seen working out in a gym and later walking out with his friends. A film song can be heard in the background meaning: “I will definitely kill… make arrangements to save yourself…” It is being said that the video was made a few days before the incident. Police suspect there was already enmity between the two sides. Investigators believe he made such a reel to display dominance. stories.title: Woman pushes friend’s son into canal, kills him:35-year friendship ends in murder, took boy on scooter ride in Saharanpur
stories.summary: A woman in Saharanpur has been arrested for allegedly murdering her friend’s 14-year-old son following a dispute over ₹6 lakh, police said. On May 1, she reportedly lured the boy who was outside his house, onto her scooter on the pretext of taking him for a ride. She then took him about 8 km away to a canal and pushed him in. When the child did not return, his family began searching and later filed a missing person report. During the investigation, CCTV footage showed the woman taking the boy on her scooter. Police arrested her the same day, and she confessed to the crime. The boy’s body was recovered from the canal on Saturday. The incident falls under the City police station area. See 3 pictures- Read the complete story of a 15-year friendship turning sour and murder Bal Krishna Bharti lives with his family in the Numaish Camp area. The family consists of his wife Jyoti and 4 sons - Anurag, Vishal, Vikas, and Anshuman (14). Anurag was the eldest, and Anshuman was the youngest. In their neighborhood, a woman named Pooja (42) lives alone in her house. She is a 35-year-old friend of Bal Krishna's wife. According to the police, both families used to visit each other's homes. Pooja had recently sold one of her shops to Jyoti's eldest son, Anurag, for ₹6 lakhs. It was agreed that the money would be paid later. After a few days, a dispute started between them over the money. Pooja alleges that Jyoti and her family members were not paying the money. There was also a quarrel between them over this. Then communication between them stopped. Pooja was very angry about this. She plotted revenge. On May 1, she saw Jyoti's son, Anshuman, roaming around. She called him over, made him sit on her scooter, took him away, and killed him. Woman seen taking child on scooter in CCTV When Anshuman did not return home for a long time, the family became suspicious. They filed a complaint with the police. When police checked nearby CCTV footage, a woman was seen taking Anshuman away on a scooter. The family identified the woman as Pooja. After this, the police took her into custody from her home. Child's body found floating in canal after 2 days When police interrogated her strictly, Pooja revealed that she had pushed the child into the canal. On Saturday, a rescue operation was conducted in the main canal based on her identification. Two divers searched throughout the day, but the child could not be located. On Sunday, passersby near the canal saw the child's body floating in the water and informed the police. Upon receiving the information, the police reached the spot. Anshuman's family members were also called, who identified the body. The police have sent the body for a post-mortem. Accused woman said- I got scared During police interrogation, Pooja said that I had no such intention. I just got scared because his family members were calling repeatedly. They were asking about Anshuman. I panicked because of this. His mother and brother also used to fight with me often. I had no enmity with him. Brother alleges revenge over past dispute The victim’s elder brother, Anurag, said his 14-year-old brother Anshuman went missing from Chhota Chowk on May 1 at 2:04 PM, and his body was found the next morning. He alleged that the accused, Pooja, took revenge for a dispute that took place about one and a half years ago. He said Pooja used to visit their house and had earlier behaved aggressively with the children, which the family had opposed. According to him, she had even threatened to “teach them a lesson,” and has now carried out that threat. He demanded strict justice in the case. Councillor flags misleading statements by accused Councillor Rahul Jham said he was informed by a local resident that a woman named Pooja had taken the child. During questioning, her responses appeared suspicious as she kept giving different locations, including Sarasawa, Yamunanagar, and Thanabhawan. He said the accused misled the police throughout the night, but during strict interrogation, she confessed that on the evening of May 1, around 8 PM, she pushed the child into a canal. He demanded strict action, calling such individuals a threat to society. Police detail investigation and recovery SP City Vyom Bindal said a missing person complaint was received from the Numaish Camp area, after which a case was registered, and a search operation began. CCTV footage showed a woman taking the child away, helping police identify and trace the accused through surveillance. During questioning, the woman confessed to throwing the child into a canal on Ambala Road. A team of over 17 divers was deployed, and the canal flow was temporarily stopped. After nearly 17 hours of effort, the body was recovered on Saturday morning around 6 AM. Police said the accused and the victim’s family had known each other for about 10 years, but had been in dispute for the past one and a half years over financial dealings related to a shop. Investigators believe the murder was carried out as an act of revenge.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:IRGC says, 'Trump left with limited choices'; Yogi announces 1.5 lakh recruitments in UP this year more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. IRGC says Trump left with limited choices A Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) owned by National Iranian Tanker Company has reportedly evaded a US Navy blockade and reached the Asia-Pacific region carrying over 1.9 million barrels of crude oil worth nearly $220 million. 2. Yogi announces 1.5 lakh recruitments in UP this year UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday announced that 1.5 lakh recruitments will be carried out in the state within a year. Speaking in Lucknow, he said the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) alone will conduct around 32,000 recruitments, while the Education Selection Commission will also hire thousands of teachers. 3. Air Force rescues 2 children using MI-17 Helicopter, 5 children climbed water tank In Siddharthnagar, Uttar Pradesh, children who were stranded on a water tank for 16 hours were rescued by the Air Force using an MI-17 helicopter. Both were admitted to the Air Force hospital in Gorakhpur. On Saturday, 5 children climbed a 60-foot-high water tank in the Kashiram Awas Colony to make a reel. While getting down, the ladder broke. 3 children fell down. 4. Suvendu Adhikari alleges leak of counting duty details The Election Commission has ordered fresh polling across all 285 polling booths of the Falta assembly seat of South 24 Parganas of West Bengal on May 21. BJP leader and Bengal's LoP Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday alleged that several officers deployed for counting day duties are reportedly disclosing their duty details, locations and designations to their departmental organisations and associations, terming it a serious breach of election protocol. 5. Soil mound collapse in Kaushambi kills 3, 2 rescued A sudden collapse of a mud mound in Kaushambi at around 7 am on Sunday left 5 people buried under debris. In the accident, three people, including a mother and daughter, died on the spot. Police and administrative officials rushed to the site after receiving information and launched a rescue operation. 6. IAS officer Rinku Singh still awaits posting after withdrawing resignation Uttar Pradesh cadre IAS officer Rinku Singh Rahi has not received a posting even 13 days after withdrawing his resignation on April 20, raising questions over administrative delays. The 2021-batch officer said he is willing to serve anywhere but does not feel comfortable drawing a salary without work. 7. Massive fire in Delhi's Shahadara building leaves 9 dead A fire broke out in a 4-storey building in Vivek Vihar, Shahdara of New Delhi, resulting in the death of nine people on Sunday. So far, 3-4 bodies have been found. And around 15 people have been rescued, including two who suffered minor injuries. 8. Woman climbs water tank, threatens to commit suicide A 32-year-old woman, Pallavi Singh, climbed a 50-foot-high water tank in Prayagraj on Saturday around 1 PM and threatened to end her life. From the top, she shouted that a case registered against her was false and said she would not come down until it was withdrawn. 9. Content creators build ₹50,000 crore digital economy Shivani Kumari from Auraiya became viral after she mistakenly said ‘Hello Frenda’ instead of ‘Hello Friend’ in a video. Her unique speaking style became her identity. Today, her net worth runs into crores. Then there is Shadab Jakati from Meerut, who once worked as a driver in Saudi Arabia. He became famous with a simple video asking, “How much is the Rs 10 biscuit, sir?” 10. Mittal family buys Rajasthan Royals in ₹15,660 cr deal Industrialists Lakshmi N. Mittal and Aditya Mittal have agreed to acquire Rajasthan Royals with Adar Poonawalla as partner, valuing the franchise at $1.65 billion (₹15,660).

stories.title: Construction of 108 accommodations begins in PAC:Subedar Nayak performs Bhoomi Pujan; officials say personnel will get better facilities
stories.summary: The construction work of 108 special type residences at the 37th Battalion PAC located in Shyamnagar, Kanpur, was inaugurated. Deputy Commandant Tanu Upadhyay (ADSP) formally commenced this project by performing Bhoomi Pujan with Vedic chanting. This initiative has been taken towards providing better residential arrangements for the battalion personnel and expanding basic facilities. Under the direction of Commandant B.B. Chaurasia, a groundbreaking and Panchshila Pujan ceremony was organized for the 'construction of Special Type First residences'. Officers and staff present on this occasion expressed happiness at the commencement of the construction work. They said that the new residences would provide better residential facilities to the battalion's officers and staff, which would have a positive impact on their work performance. After the Pujan ceremony, prasad was distributed among all present officers, staff members, and representatives of the executing agency (UPPPCL). Under the leadership of Commandant B.B. Chaurasia, continuous development and construction work are being carried out in the 37th Battalion PAC. Officers stated that work is progressing in a planned manner for the all-round development of the battalion premises, so that personnel can receive modern and better facilities in the future. The Bhoomi Pujan (ground-breaking) ceremony was attended by Chandreshwar (Camp Pal), Manoj Kumar Srivastava (RTC In-charge), Arvindra Kumar (Squad Leader G Squad), Ravendra Singh Chaudhary (Subedar Military Assistant), Shivangshu Dwivedi (SQM), Vineet Tripathi (Head Clerk), along with all officers and staff of the battalion. The program was conducted in a peaceful and dignified atmosphere.

stories.title: History-sheeter beaten to death in Fatehpur:8 people attack with sticks and rods; parents were also harmed despite repeated pleas
stories.summary: A 32-year-old history-sheeter was beaten to death with sticks and clubs in Fatehpur. The video of the incident surfaced on Sunday. In the video, 8 people can be seen beating history-sheeter Abhimanyu alias Kunnu Yadav with sticks and clubs. His mother and father are trying to save him. They kept pleading before the accused, but the accused did not listen to them at all. Rather, they beat them, too. The accused fled, thinking he was dead. He died during treatment at the district hospital. The history-sheeter's parents were also injured in the attack. The entire incident took place on Friday in the Husainganj police station area, 10 km from the city. On Saturday, the police handed over the body to the family after the post-mortem. His last rites were performed in the late evening. Police investigation revealed that the history-sheeter had an ongoing dispute with gangster Kamlesh Yadav from the same village. There had been several fights between the two over dominance in the past as well. In this same rivalry, Kamlesh Yadav carried out the incident along with his family members. The police have registered a case against 10 people, including Kamlesh Yadav. History-sheeter was sitting outside the house, beaten with sticks and clubs History-sheeter Abhimanyu was a resident of Poore Rahimal Majra Jamrawan village under Husainganj police station. On Friday morning at 10 o'clock, he was sitting at the door of his house. Just then, Kamlesh Yadav came with his family members carrying sticks and clubs. Seeing them, Abhimanyu tried to run away, but they caught him. They started beating him with kicks, punches, and sticks. When the blood-soaked Abhimanyu raised an alarm, his father, Maan Singh Yadav, and mother, Nanki Devi, came running to save him. When they tried to save their son, they were also beaten, and the accused left after threatening them. The family members took the injured to the district hospital, where Abhimanyu died during treatment. Uncle Gyan Singh Yadav alleged that Kamlesh Yadav, Manish, and Sachin from the village beat his nephew Abhimanyu to death due to an old rivalry. History-sheeter had 20 to 25 cases registered against him SP Abhimanyu Manglik said in the initial investigation that Kunnu Yadav was a history-sheeter of the police station. 20 to 25 cases were registered against him. Cases are also registered against his brother and father. Kunnu Yadav's mental condition was not stable. A notice was sent to the family from the police station regarding this. The notice stated that your son's mental condition is not stable. He used to quarrel frequently, which posed a threat to peace in the area. He had been advised to be admitted to a mental hospital. A day before the incident, on Thursday, Kunnu Yadav had a dispute with the accused. After this, the accused carried out the crime. A video of the murder has surfaced. Based on this, the accused will be arrested as soon as possible.

stories.title: Protests against smart meters spread across 5 UP cities:Residents allege inflated bills, power cuts despite payments; AAP workers clash with Lucknow police
stories.summary: Opposition to smart meters is growing in UP. On Sunday, protests regarding smart meters took place in Agra, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Lucknow, and Varanasi. In Agra, women uprooted smart meters from their homes and threw them on the streets. They said, "We don't want smart meters, we want the old meters. Since the installation of smart meters, electricity bills have been higher. Money is being deposited in advance. Even after depositing money, electricity is being cut. When inquired, they say the balance is in minus''. A protest had also taken place here 2 days ago. Scuffle with police in Lucknow, dragged away The AAP party held a strong protest. AAP workers reached Shakti Bhawan carrying posters and placards in their hands in Lucknow. They started moving towards the Assembly while raising slogans against the BJP government. The police stopped the protesters near Shriram Tower. The protesters insisted on moving forward. This led to a sharp confrontation with the police. The police took them into custody. They were dragged and put into vehicles and taken to Eco Garden. Pratipal Singh, who participated in the protest, has alleged that his turban was pulled off to humiliate him. AAP spokesperson in Varanasi said - We will continue to protest Aam Aadmi Party protested against smart meters at Chaukaghat electricity substation in Varanasi. Spokesperson Mukesh Singh said that common people are being harassed by smart meters. We will continue to protest against it at all costs. Because its bill is being taken arbitrarily. The government should stop it immediately, because it is smartly cheating people. Why is there opposition to smart meters? Read on Electricity consumers say that smart meters run very fast. This results in higher bills even with less usage. Sometimes the balance decreases even without usage. As soon as the balance goes into minus, the electricity supply is cut off. Even after a recharge, the supply is often not restored immediately. After months of opposition to smart meters, the state government issued a new order. According to this, it was stated that electricity would not be cut off for connections up to 1 kilowatt for 30 days, and for 2 kilowatt connections, even if the balance goes minus by ₹200.

stories.summary: UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday announced that 1.5 lakh recruitments will be carried out in the state within a year. Speaking in Lucknow, he said the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) alone will conduct around 32,000 recruitments, while the Education Selection Commission will also hire thousands of teachers. He added that the Public Service Commission will provide about 15,000 jobs. The UP Police Recruitment and Promotion Board is currently recruiting 45,000 Home Guards and Sub-Inspectors, with a similar number of vacancies expected in the near future. Overall, around 1.5 lakh appointments will be made in 2026–27 through various commissions and boards. During the event, CM Yogi distributed appointment letters to 357 Junior Analysts (Medicine) and 252 Dental Hygienists selected by UPSSSC. He also took a swipe at past practices, alleging that earlier recruitment processes were marred by corruption. He said that officials and influential figures used to engage in extortion, and stressed that it is everyone’s responsibility to stand against dishonest leaders and bureaucrats. CM narrated the story of a youth's suicide due to not getting a job The Chief Minister said he recalled an incident from his time as an MP from Gorakhpur. One evening, a highway was blocked after a young man died by suicide. The area fell within his constituency, and officials advised him not to visit due to public anger, but he chose to go. He said that when people saw him, the situation calmed down. He spoke to the crowd and met the bereaved family. During his inquiry, he was told that the young man had secured a general rank in a police recruitment process but did not receive an appointment letter, which led him into depression and, eventually, to take his own life. Read Yogi's 4 big statements- 1- We have a law of life imprisonment for those who breach recruitment The CM said that a strict law has been made to ensure that no recruitment process is breached. Whoever is found guilty of fraud in recruitment, there is also a law to confiscate their property and sentence them to life imprisonment. Parents wish that their sons and daughters get a good education and a good job, but when expected results don't come, and a young person's dreams are shattered, it is not just a betrayal of that youth, but also a betrayal of the future of the coming generation. UP didn't become a BIMARU state just like that. Through discrimination and corruption in the selection process, the state was turned into a BIMARU and anarchic state. The state was plagued by hooliganism. Curfews would remain in place for months. There was discrimination in the selection process. Courts had to stop recruitments. Someone else would take the exam, and someone else would receive the appointment letter. 2- Earlier, everything was left to God; today, there are 81 medical colleges The CM said that if we leave aside four or five districts, almost all of the 75 districts in the state have medical colleges. Today, there are 81 medical colleges and two AIIMS. Earlier, there were neither colleges nor staff. Everything was left to God. Results also came accordingly. People didn't even know about the Food Safety and Drug Administration. What medicine they were taking, whether it had quality or not, there was no inspection of this. There was adulteration in everything. Who would stop it? The police could hardly stop it. The responsible department didn't have labs. Test results would take years to come. Adulterators couldn't be punished. Adulteration in milk, spices, fruits, and sweets was common. The department responsible for this work had neither adequate staff, nor labs, nor equipment. Now labs have been established at the division level for testing samples. They have equipment and manpower available. Food safety-related samples can be tested in the same commissionerate. 3- Earlier people were only concerned about their own and their family's health The Chief Minister said that now test samples are examined within a fixed time, and people are informed whether they are correct or not. Earlier, there were only five laboratories, but now 18 well-equipped labs are operational. The number of samples has increased from 12,000 earlier to 55,000 now. He added that earlier, people did not fully understand the importance of health and focused only on themselves and their families. Emphasising dental care, he said that if a tooth is damaged, it affects the taste of food. With better dental doctors now available, people will receive proper guidance, leading to improved health. 4- A lot has changed in 9 years Yogi said that significant changes have taken place over the last 9 years. He remarked that earlier, even ineligible individuals, including those with fake degrees, became commission chairpersons and oversaw recruitments, often involving corruption. As a result, recruitment processes were stalled. After his government came to power, he questioned why police recruitments were not happening and found that several cases were pending in courts. He said the process was then completed in accordance with court directions, and so far, 2.20 lakh recruitments have been made in the police department. He added that earlier the scale of work was limited, but things have changed. In 2025, when 60,244 police constables were recruited at once, many doubted whether UP could handle their training. However, the entire training was conducted within the state, and the candidates have since been deployed. Earlier, only about 3,000 constables could be trained at a time in the state.

stories.title: Groom spends 20 years’ savings on elephant wedding entry:Hires ‘royal elephant’ for ₹2.6 lakh; says dream matters, rich or poor
stories.summary: A young man from Meerut fulfilled a childhood dream by arriving at his wedding procession on an elephant instead of the traditional mare. Ankit had dreamed of this since the age of five and had shared it with his father and grandfather. Taking his wish seriously, the family ensured that his dream would come true. On April 21, Ankit’s wedding procession travelled from Jamalpur to Mandaura village with him seated on an elephant. Before heading to the bride’s village, Ankit rode through his own village on the elephant. The unique sight drew large crowds, with villagers gathering to watch the unusual procession. The wedding, from Jamalpur village under Inchauli police station area, has since become a talking point in the region. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Ankit said, “A dream is a dream. Whether one is rich or poor, everyone has the right to fulfil it. My dream was to bring my bride home while riding an elephant, and today it has come true.” First, see these pictures... Read the complete conversation with Ankit and his father... A family living in a hut-like house Ankit's father name is Kalu. There are a total of 6 children in the family, including 4 daughters and 2 sons. Ankit lives with his family in Jamalpur village. Their house is a kutcha (temporary structure). Many rooms don't even have a roof. The entire family lives in the open in a hut-like house. Ankit's father works as a laborer. Ankit also works cutting sugarcane in fields and doing labor work. He gets a daily wage of about ₹500 rupees. The family's expenses are managed with this. He has done ITI after 12th standard. He has recently given the Railway exam. He is also preparing for several other competitive examinations. First got younger siblings married Ankit said that I never took away my siblings' rights for my dreams. First, I got my younger brother married. He had a love marriage. He has three children and lives separately. My two elder sisters are also married. Now, I live with my grandfather, father, mother, and two younger sisters. Only after the marriage of two sisters and my younger brother did I think about my own marriage, so that there would be no pressure on anyone. The relationship happened with family consent Ankit said that my dream was to take out the wedding procession riding on an elephant. To fulfill this desire, I invested all my savings. My marriage is with Pooja, who lives in Mandaura village of Muzaffarnagar. This is an arranged marriage. We also got an elephant's picture printed on the wedding card, which made people quite excited. When I reached the girl's village with the wedding procession riding on an elephant, the people there also liked my style very much. Elephant came from Rajasthan for two and a half lakh rupees Ankit said that we wanted a royal elephant as we needed. It was not available in Meerut or nearby. On asking people, we found out that good elephants are available in Jaipur, Rajasthan. After that, we searched on Google. We got the number of Imran Bhai from Jaipur, who provides elephants for weddings. We booked the elephant online and called it to Meerut. The elephant's rent and travel expenses were around ₹1 lakh 60 thousand. It cost approximately ₹1 lakh for the permission to bring the elephant from Rajasthan to Meerut. Thus, the total expenditure came to ₹2 lakh 60 thousand. The company people themselves brought the food items for the elephant. They had specified some things for the elephant, which we arranged here. Now, my wife and I, and the entire family, are very happy. Elephant brought from Rajasthan in a truck The elephant reached Ankit's house from Rajasthan on April 21 at around 2 PM. It was brought in a truck. After reaching home, a ceremony was held in the village. Ankit, dressed as a groom with a turban on his head and a sword in his hand, rode the elephant. The elephant was taken around the entire village. After this, the elephant was taken by truck to Mandaura village in Muzaffarnagar. Outside the village, Ankit again sat on the elephant and reached the bride's house with the wedding procession. There too, people appeared quite excited seeing the elephant. After the wedding rituals, at around 2 AM at night, the elephant was sent back from Muzaffarnagar to Jaipur by truck itself. Father say happy that son's wish was fulfilled Ankit's father, Kalu, said, "My son had decided in his childhood that he would sit on an elephant as a groom. That's when we also resolved that his wedding procession would go on an elephant, no matter what it takes." "Ankit and I saved for about 20 years for this. We worked hard and did labor to collect this amount. With that money, we called an elephant and took the wedding procession with my son sitting on the elephant. Today I am happy that we could fulfill his dream." Such a sight seen after 75 years In old times, there was a tradition among the elite of taking out wedding processions on elephants. According to local people, such a sight was seen in the area after about 75 years, when a groom took out a wedding procession riding on an elephant. It is said that before this, in the year 1951, the wedding procession of Delhi resident Niranjan Gupta had come to Lavad. At that time, too, the groom had arrived with the wedding procession riding on an elephant.

stories.title: Woman climbs water tank, threatens to commit suicide:Claims case against her is false; refuses to come down until withdrawn
stories.summary: A 32-year-old woman, Pallavi Singh, climbed a 50-foot-high water tank in Prayagraj on Saturday around 1 PM and threatened to end her life. From the top, she shouted that a case registered against her was false and said she would not come down until it was withdrawn. As her voice drew attention, hundreds of people gathered at the spot. Police reached the scene and tried to persuade her to come down, assuring her that appropriate action would be taken after an investigation. Pallavi remained atop the tank for nearly 9 hours, creating a tense situation. She finally came down around 10 PM, after which the police took her to the station. The incident took place in the Phaphamau area, about 15 km from the city. During the investigation, police found that Pallavi had a love marriage with Mohammad Alam. Her husband had filed a fraud case against her at the Phaphamau police station, following which Pallavi also lodged a case against him. See 3 pictures of the girl's drama... A day before, a picture with notes had surfaced Pallavi Singh is originally a resident of Ballia. She currently lives in Phaphamau. A day before, her picture had surfaced on social media, in which she was lying on a bed covered with ₹500-500 rupee notes and using her mobile phone. On Saturday at one o'clock in the afternoon, she climbed up a 50-foot-high water tank built near Basna drain in Phaphamau. People present there thought that the young woman had gone to talk on the phone. But eyewitnesses said that the girl broke the lock of the ladder and went up. After this, a crowd gathered there. Meanwhile, a passerby woman climbed up the tank to counsel the young woman. But the young woman started a Facebook live. The young woman said that I have become a victim of love jihad, I have consumed poison. The police filed a case against me. Don't motivate me, go away from here. After this, she drove the woman away, threatening to jump. 'Theft is being orchestrated at my house daily' Coming live on Facebook, the young woman Pallavi made serious allegations against the Phaphamau Inspector. She said that Alam (husband), a relative of Atiq Ahmad, along with other people, files cases against me every day. I have been greatly harassed by the Prayagraj administration; I have no option left except suicide. Theft is being orchestrated at my house daily, to the extent that the Phaphamau Inspector himself broke into my house and committed theft in 2024. ACP Tharwai reached the spot after 1 hour About 1 hour later, at 2 PM, ACP Tharwai reached the spot and tried to bring her down by calling out through a microphone. Around 3 PM, he himself climbed onto the tank to persuade the young woman, but even after hours of convincing, she did not come down. Meanwhile, the young woman was continuously live on Facebook and was also talking on a call from another phone. The young woman shouted from above and said that the crowd should be removed from here, and a case should be registered against my husband, Alam, and he should be sent to jail. Even after this, the ACP kept trying to persuade her. She kept threatening to jump and end her life. Finally, around 10 PM at night, after getting assurance that all her conditions would be met, she somehow came down with the ACP. Station House Officer Kambod Singh informed - Several cases are already registered against Pallavi in different police stations. She is being interrogated regarding the picture that surfaced with the currency notes.
