stories.title: Soldier kills wife at girlfriend's behest:Befriends 11 years younger girl on Facebook; says, ‘Kill her if you want to be with me’
stories.summary: A soldier killed his wife for his girlfriend in Bareilly. Police revealed that the soldier used to give ₹15k every month to his girlfriend, whom he met on Facebook, to support her expenses. However, when the girlfriend found out that the soldier was married, a fight started between them. After this, the girlfriend told the soldier that if you want to stay with me, you will have to kill your wife. Blinded by love, the soldier strangled his wife to death on April 22 at his girlfriend's behest. After the incident, the soldier called and told his girlfriend everything. Based on CCTV and call details, police arrested the girlfriend on May 1. On the same day, the accused soldier surrendered in court. The case is from the Subhash Nagar police station area. CCTV footage that revealed the secret Now read the entire matter in detail sequentially.... Met on Facebook 5 years ago Originally a resident of Badaun, Bharat Singh (35) was living in Geeta Colony, Bareilly. He had built a house here a year ago. Bharat Singh Yadav was posted in the army in Firozpur, Punjab. 16 years ago, Bharat Singh married Geeta Yadav (32). They have two children, Drishya (14) and Harsh (12). Both children study in the Army School. About 5 years ago, Bharat Singh met Surbhi Yadav (24), a resident of Badaun, on Facebook. Bharat introduced himself as a bachelor. The two became friends, and gradually this friendship turned into love. The two started talking for hours on the phone. Bharat started sending ₹14-15k to Surbhi every month. However, when Surbhi came to know that Bharat was married and had two children, disputes started between them. Called girlfriend after the murder During this time, Surbhi laid down a condition that if he wanted to live with her, he would have to kill his wife. Only after that would he be able to live with her. On April 18, Bharat Singh took leave and reached Badaun. There, both of them together decided that Geeta should be murdered so that they could get married. On the night of April 21, Bharat left from Surbhi's place and reached Bareilly around 4:00 AM on April 22. At 11:15 AM during the day, he came to his house. With a towel tied around his face and holding an umbrella in his hand, he entered the house so that his identity could be hidden. Geeta was alone at home, and both children had gone to school. Bharat brutally strangled Geeta to death and fled from the scene. After the murder, he immediately called Surbhi and informed her about it. However, the entire incident was captured on CCTV camera. Secret revealed through CCTV and call details Accused tried to hide his identity, but the children recognized him from his walk in the CCTV footage. After this, the police intensified the investigation based on call details and surveillance. On May 1, the police arrested Surbhi Yadav, while Bharat Singh surrendered in court. Used to beat mother daily The son, Drishya, revealed that there were frequent fights between mom and dad. Dad used to talk to a girl. When mom would forbid him from doing so, dad would beat her. A day before the murder, Dad had called and said that you must go to school tomorrow. The son said with a choked voice that if I had even the slightest idea that Dad would kill Mom, I would have never gone to school that day. Drishya revealed that her dad had been hiding in Bareilly for several days, but had lied at home that he was on duty. Deceived the unit too in the name of leave The investigation revealed that Bharat Singh had taken leave from his unit starting April 17 by showing a fake wedding card. He told his family he was in Jammu, while he was actually staying in Bareilly. SP City Manush Pareek stated- Based on CCTV and surveillance, suspicion deepened on the accused husband. The investigation revealed the girlfriend's role in the murder conspiracy, after which she has been arrested. The main accused will be taken on remand for further action.

stories.title: Air Force rescues 2 children using MI-17 Helicopter:5 children climbed water tank to shoot reel; 3 fell after ladder collapsed, 1 dead
stories.summary: In Siddharthnagar, Uttar Pradesh, children who were stranded on a water tank for 16 hours were rescued by the Air Force using an MI-17 helicopter. Both were admitted to the Air Force hospital in Gorakhpur. On Saturday, 5 children climbed a 60-foot-high water tank in the Kashiram Awas Colony to make a reel. While getting down, the ladder broke. 3 children fell down. Out of these, 1 died, while 2 are in critical condition. 2 children hung onto rods and then slowly climbed back onto the tank. Due to the marshy area around the tank, difficulties were faced in the rescue operation. A hydraulic crane was called, but it could not reach the tank due to the swamp. Therefore, work to build a 150-meter road was started. By late night, about 120 meters of the road had been constructed. Meanwhile, around 3 am, heavy rain started, forcing the work to stop. Considering the situation, the administration sought help from the army. After this, on Sunday morning at around 5:20 am, an Air Force MI-17 helicopter reached the spot. Both children were rescued safely. First, understand the entire incident in a sequential manner… In the Kashiram Awas Colony located at the district headquarters, Bale (12), a resident of Mohana, had come to his maternal cousin Deepchand’s house. On Saturday, around 3 pm, he, along with Golu (15), Shani (11), Kallu (15), and Pawan (16) from the neighborhood, climbed a dilapidated water tank near the housing colony to make a reel. After staying on top for a while, all of them started coming down one by one. Suddenly, after descending just four steps, the dilapidated ladder broke. As a result, Bale, Shani, and Golu fell down. Debris from the ladder fell on Bale, causing his death on the spot. Shani and Golu were injured. Kallu and Pawan got stranded on top. After the incident, chaos broke out at the spot. Nearby people rushed to the scene. In a hurry, people carried the injured in their arms and took them to the hospital, where doctors declared Bale dead. After receiving information, DM Shivsharanappa GN and SSP Abhishek Mahajan, along with several officials, reached the spot. Relief and rescue operations were initiated. A poclain machine was called to clear the debris.

stories.title: Soil mound collapses, 3 dead including mother-daughter:2 rescued, accident during excavation in Kaushambi
stories.summary: A sudden collapse of a mud mound in Kaushambi at around 7 am on Sunday left 5 people buried under debris. In the accident, three people, including a mother and daughter, died on the spot. Police and administrative officials rushed to the site after receiving information and launched a rescue operation. The accident took place while soil was being excavated from a pond. Suddenly, a large mound of mud caved in and came crashing down, trapping those working below it. Panic spread instantly, with screams heard across the area. Local residents rushed to help, triggering scenes of chaos and urgency. Villagers and police are jointly carrying out rescue efforts and pulling out the injured from under the debris. They are being shifted to a nearby hospital for treatment. The deceased have been identified as Uttara Devi, Geeta Devi and Bitti. The bodies have been taken into custody and sent for post-mortem. The accident occurred in Chakthama village under Manjhanpur tehsil. See pictures-

stories.title: Creators turn crorepatis by making videos online:Build ₹50,000-crore digital economy; earnings go up to ₹4.5 lakh a month
stories.summary: Shivani Kumari from Auraiya became viral after she mistakenly said ‘Hello Frenda’ instead of ‘Hello Friend’ in a video. Her unique speaking style became her identity. Today, her net worth runs into crores. Then there is Shadab Jakati from Meerut, who once worked as a driver in Saudi Arabia. He became famous with a simple video asking, “How much is the Rs 10 biscuit, sir?” The clip went so viral that rapper Badshah and cricketer Rinku Singh made videos on the same theme. These are just two names. Uttar Pradesh now has thousands of content creators whose lives have been transformed by social media. Many of them would have struggled to secure jobs paying even Rs 10,000 to Rs 20,000 a month. Today, by making videos, they are earning between Rs 4 lakh and Rs 4.5 lakh every month. Estimates suggest that the social media content business in UP alone has grown into a Rs 50,000-crore annual industry, while across India, it is now worth nearly Rs 3 lakh crore. In today’s Sunday Big Story, here is a look at how creators earn from video content, how ordinary people are becoming celebrities, and what different social media platforms offer. Became a hit with the slipper video, today a millionaire Shivani’s journey as a content creator is remarkable. She once worked as a farm labourer. In 2018, while going to the market to buy slippers for her sister’s children, she made a video and accidentally said ‘Hello Frenda’. The video went massively viral on TikTok, and by 2020, Shivani had gained 50 lakh followers. After TikTok was banned, she shifted to Instagram, YouTube and Facebook. Her first earnings were Rs 20,000. She mainly creates videos around daily life and village routines. When asked whether she can now be called a crorepati, Shivani smiled hesitantly and said, “Yes… you can say that now.” Kapil is promoting several brands in IPL Kapil Kanpuriya from Kanpur, whose real name is Kapil Shukla, once went to Mumbai hoping to become an actor. After failing there, he returned and took up an accountant’s job in Gurugram in 2017. When the lockdown began in 2020, Kapil started making videos on relatable topics such as how to recover borrowed money and how to complain to a company’s HR department. His content quickly connected with people. He later brought his mother Pushpa and wife Kirti into his videos. Family-based content made him hugely popular, and today several companies approach him for brand promotions. During the IPL, Kapil was seen promoting multiple brands. His monthly earnings have now reached lakhs. Rapper Badshah, cricketer Rinku Singh among many celebrities following Shadab, from Inchauli town in Meerut, had worked as a driver in Saudi Arabia. After returning to UP, he shot a video at a local shop on 15 May 2025, asking: “How much is the Rs 10 biscuit, sir?” The video exploded online, drawing 89 million views on Instagram. His theme was later copied by celebrities including rapper Badshah and cricketer Rinku Singh. Today, companies in Delhi, Meerut and Ghaziabad regularly approach Shadab for promotions, paying him lakhs of rupees. Recently, he even opened a jewellery showroom in Meerut. Though controversies have also surrounded his name, his popularity remains high. Jackie Yadav from Etawah has 4 lakh followers on X. He earns nearly Rs 2 lakh every month from X alone, apart from brand promotion income. Jackie said, “I was preparing for UPSC CSE till 2021. In 2022, I started writing on political and social issues through my account. By the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, more than one crore people were reading me every day.” He added, “People now see me as a trendsetter. I currently have a team of three people helping with research. My name featured in the Top-20 ranking list related to X. With social media earnings, I bought a Thar and a Brezza.” How Can You Earn from Different Platforms? YouTube Channel Need 1,000 X (formerly Twitter) You can get 2000 to 3000 rupees for one million views Social media platform X, earlier known as Twitter, was bought by Elon Musk on 27 October 2022 for 44 billion dollars. From July 2023, X introduced payouts for creators. To qualify, creators need X Premium, which costs Rs 472 a month, and gives a blue tick. To become eligible for payouts, an account must achieve: Once eligible, creators can earn 25 to 30 dollars per one million views. However, X payouts depend heavily on how many verified users engage with your post. X pays every 14 days. If during that period your account records: then earnings can touch 150 dollars. Content Creator Economy Will Reach $1 Lakh Crore A big question remains—how many content creators are there in India? At the WAVES Summit in Mumbai in May 2025, it was stated that India has 20 to 25 lakh creators with more than 1,000 followers. A Boston Consulting Group report says only 8 to 10% of content creators are currently making money—roughly 2 lakh to 2.5 lakh people. The rest either earn very little or are still trying to monetise their content. In March 2025, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said: “We will create a 100-crore-dollar arrangement for the creator economy.” Social Media Platforms Make the Real Money It is also worth noting that in 2025, YouTube earned Rs 34,742 crore from India, while Meta, through Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, earned nearly Rs 29,392 crore. Creators may be making money—but the biggest profits are still flowing to social media companies.

stories.title: IAS who made clerk do sit-ups still awaits posting:Says ‘no calls received’; retired IAS calls it government’s discretion
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh cadre IAS officer Rinku Singh Rahi has not received a posting even 13 days after withdrawing his resignation on April 20, raising questions over administrative delays. The 2021-batch officer said he is willing to serve anywhere but does not feel comfortable drawing a salary without work. Speaking to Bhaskar, Rahi said, “I just want work. Wherever the government posts me, it doesn’t matter. Taking salary without working does not feel right.” Currently, Rahi has been attached to the Revenue Council, headed by Chairman Anil Kumar. Sources said he was recently assigned departmental work by the chairman, which he has completed. However, no formal posting order has been issued so far. No clarity on posting, no calls from officials Rahi said there is still no clarity regarding his role after withdrawing his resignation. “I haven’t demanded any specific posting. I only want to work,” he said, adding that while he received several calls after submitting his resignation, no official has contacted him since he withdrew it. He confirmed that he continues to receive full salary while on attachment but reiterated discomfort over being without responsibilities for nearly nine months. IAS Rinku Singh Rahi on posting delay Question: What process is underway after you withdrew your resignation? Answer: It is not very clear what is happening in my case right now. I have not made any demand for posting; I just want to work. Question: Did you receive a call from any officer? Answer: After submitting my resignation, I received many calls. But after withdrawing it, no officer has contacted me. Question: So are you receiving your salary? Answer: I am on attachment and receiving full salary. Question: You resigned because you were getting salary without work, right? Answer: I have not had any work for the past nine months. That is why taking salary without work does not feel right. I want a posting so that I can do some work. Attachment has no fixed timeline, says retired IAS officer A retired IAS officer said that in such cases, it is entirely the government’s discretion to keep an officer on attachment while awaiting posting orders. There is no fixed timeline for this process. The government may appoint an APO (Assistant Prosecution Officer) if it chooses. However, traditionally, officers are given postings within a few months. Met senior officials, still awaiting posting IAS officer Rinku Singh Rahi has met Chief Secretary SP Goyal, Revenue Council Chairman Anil Kumar, and Additional Chief Secretary (Personnel) M. Devraj. He briefed them about recent developments and requested a posting so he could work for the public. However, no posting has been given so far. Abhishek Prakash case highlights contrast Retired IAS officers point out that Abhishek Prakash, former CEO of Invest UP, was suspended on March 20, 2025, over bribery allegations. After the High Court quashed the chargesheet, he was reinstated on March 14, 2026, and was given a posting the very next day as Secretary in the General Administration Department. IAS officer removed after sit-up controversy 44-year-old Rinku Singh Rahi, a 2021-batch IAS officer, still has around 16 years of service left but has been without a field posting for the past nine months. He was removed from Shahjahanpur and attached to the Revenue Council after a controversy during his tenure as SDM of Puwaiyan tehsil. Rahi earlier served as Joint Magistrate in Mathura before taking charge as SDM in Puwaiyan at 2 pm on July 24, 2025. During an inspection, he noticed Vijay (38), a clerk of a lawyer, using a spot near a wall as a toilet inside the premises. He stopped him and directed him to use proper facilities. The clerk responded that the toilets were dirty. This angered the SDM, who blamed tehsil staff and made the clerk do sit-ups on the spot. At the same time, lawyers were protesting on the premises. When they learned about the incident, they confronted the SDM. Rahi told them the clerk had made a mistake, but the lawyers objected, saying such punishment was inappropriate. They challenged him, asking if he could do sit-ups himself. Rahi replied there was no shame in it and performed five sit-ups. A video of the incident later surfaced, triggering backlash, after which he was removed and attached to the Revenue Council. ‘System needs fixing, not exit’: Rinku Singh Rahi Following the controversy, Rahi wrote to the President on March 26 seeking a technical resignation. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, he clarified that it should not be seen as quitting service but as a request or option. “If I am not being allowed to work in this position, I should be sent back to my original service (PCS),” he said. Rahi was a PCS officer before being inducted into the IAS and now wants to return to the PCS cadre. He maintains that he does not want to leave public service but believes there are systemic shortcomings that need to be addressed. “Some officers leave the system, but I want to stay and improve it,” he said.

stories.title: Western disturbance to turn active after 48 hours:Winds sweep west UP, crops get damaged by rain
stories.summary: Temperatures had dropped across Uttar Pradesh due to rainfall over the past 48 hours, but bright sunshine returned on Saturday, pushing mercury levels up by 2 to 3 degrees Celsius once again. The Meteorological Department has said that another western disturbance is likely to become active in the next 48 hours. Crops damaged by rain, Yogi says - Officers should go to the field Rainfall has caused damage to crops across Uttar Pradesh, with vegetable crops being the worst affected. Farmers fear maximum damage to cucumber, gherkin, muskmelon and watermelon crops. They say continuous moisture after rainfall could cause crops to rot. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to provide compensation to farmers affected by rain damage. He has asked officers to go to the fields, carry out an on-ground survey of losses, and submit a report to the government at the earliest so that farmers can receive timely and appropriate compensation. Weather pictures- Rain hits crops again, CM orders immediate ground survey Rain has damaged crops in several districts, especially vegetables. Crops such as cucumber, gherkin, muskmelon and watermelon are feared to have suffered the most. Farmers say excess moisture could lead to rotting. CM Yogi has ordered compensation for affected farmers and directed officials to visit fields, assess the damage and quickly submit their reports so that relief can be provided without delay. In Farrukhabad, it rained for 30 minutes on Thursday night. More than 1,000 sacks of wheat kept in the mandi got soaked. Now know what the meteorologist said According to senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh from the Regional Meteorological Centre, the impact of the outgoing western disturbance has largely ended. Except for isolated light drizzle in some Terai areas, most parts of the state witnessed clear and dry weather on Saturday. He said temperatures are expected to rise by 4 to 6 degrees Celsius before another round of rain begins from May 4 under the influence of a fresh western disturbance, likely bringing thunderstorms and rain across the state. What will the weather be like for the next 5 days? This Year's Rainfall Under the Shadow of El Nino Between June and September this year, Uttar Pradesh, along with the rest of the country, may receive below-normal rainfall. Director General of Meteorology Dr M Mahapatra said signs indicate that La Nina-like conditions in the Pacific Ocean are ending and the system is gradually shifting towards El Nino, which is associated with reduced rainfall. This suggests that this year’s southwest monsoon could remain weaker than normal. He also said reduced snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere between January and March this year may further impact the monsoon. Know About El Nino and La Nina-

stories.title: Agra wedding turns chaotic:Groom throws garland, flees as woman claims he is her husband; high-voltage drama lasted for 2 hours
stories.summary: During the Jaimala ceremony in Agra, the groom threw away the garland and ran off the stage after seeing a woman who suddenly arrived at the wedding procession of four cars, claiming, ‘The groom is my husband.’ When she created a scene, the groom’s elder brother stepped forward. The drama took a new turn when the elder brother claimed the woman was actually his wife and the groom’s sister-in-law. He alleged she had been in a relationship with his younger brother for several years and wanted to leave him to marry the groom. The high-voltage drama continued for nearly two hours, prompting most guests to flee. Meanwhile, the bride’s family was left stunned, and the bride remained seated in her wedding dress till late at night. Eventually, her family married her to another young man present there. The incident took place on Friday night in Etmadpur, about 20 km from the city. Police have taken the groom’s father and brother into custody. The wedding procession had arrived from Tundla. See 3 pictures Read the full story in detail A wedding procession from Firozabad arrived at a marriage hall in Etmadpur on Friday night. Jitendra Baghel, a resident of Mangalam City, Tundla, had arrived with his wedding procession. The wedding rituals were underway. After the Lagni and Pakki rituals, preparations for the varmala (garland exchange) were ongoing. The bride and groom had reached the stage. Both had varmalas in their hands. Before the bride and groom could exchange garlands, a woman arrived with some people in 4 cars. As soon as the woman moved towards the stage, the groom's eyes fell on her. He threw the varmala and ran off the stage. Meanwhile, the woman reached near the stage. Creating a commotion, she said, ‘He is my husband.’ As soon as the woman shouted this, the wedding guests and the bride's family were stunned. The DJ was stopped, and the dancing feet of the performers came to a halt. In no time, an argument broke out between the people who came with the woman and some of the wedding guests. The woman kept insisting that the groom, Jitendra, was her husband. Meanwhile, the family informed the police. The police arrived. They took the groom's brother and father into custody and brought them to the police station. Groom's brother said, ‘The woman is my wife’ After reaching the police station, a second twist came in the story. In front of the police, the groom's brother, Nem Singh, claimed that the woman was his wife. Both were married in 2018. But the brother-in-law and sister-in-law have been having an affair for several years. The brother claimed that his wife accuses him of being impotent and wants to marry his brother. Bride marries another man at venue During this dispute of the groom's family, silence fell over the wedding ceremony. Some people from the groom's and bride's side had a conversation. It was decided that this marriage would not take place. After this, the bride was married to another young man present at the same ceremony. He was known to the bride's side. This wedding ritual took place simply at a different location within the same premises. Etmadpur Station In-charge Alok Kumar Singh said, Police arrived on the information of a woman. The woman accused the groom of a second marriage. The groom had fled from the spot. The groom's father and brother have been taken into custody. The matter is being investigated. The bride's side has not filed any complaint.

stories.title: High-tension current spreads in Bareilly homes, claims 2 lives:Residents allege officials ignored repeated complaint of damaged transformer
stories.summary: Due to alleged gross negligence by the electricity department in Bareilly, two families in the same village lost their loved ones after current from a high-tension line entered the household supply and spread through the area. In the accident at Sudanpur village, an 11th-class student and a differently-abled young man died on the spot. While trying to save the student, his mother suffered severe burns and was admitted to hospital in critical condition. Villagers alleged they had repeatedly complained about damaged transformers and power lines and submitted applications, but officials ignored them, leading to the two deaths. Boy dies after touching electrified iron gate Subhash (16), son of Udal Singh, a resident of Sudhanpur village, was about to leave for school today morning around 7:30 am after getting ready. As soon as he touched the iron gate to step out of the house, the high-tension current running through it electrocuted him. Subhash died a painful death on the spot with a loud bang. His mother Sunita (45), who rushed to save her son, also got severely burnt after being electrocuted. She has been admitted to a private hospital in the city, where her condition remains critical. Differently-abled youth also dies In the same accident, Kunwar Pal (24) from the same village also died. Kunwar Pal was differently-abled in one leg and used to help his family by doing tailoring work at home. The sudden high voltage in the house lights did not even give him a chance to react. Kunwar Pal was the third among four brothers, and his family plunged into mourning after this incident. Villagers say that the negligence of the electricity department has turned a lively village into a cremation ground. 11,000 volt current in house's 440 volt line RP Singh, the cousin of the deceased Subhash, was present at the scene of the incident. He witnessed his brother's agonizing death right before his eyes. He said, This entire accident in our village happened due to electricity negligence. My cousin and aunt, along with the son of our other brother Vedram, were electrocuted. This all happened because an 11,000-volt high-tension line current entered the house's 440-volt line. Regarding the malfunction of this transformer, we had repeatedly informed the electricity department and public representatives, such as our MLA, in writing. Any members of the department who visited the village were repeatedly told that this transformer is faulty. Sometimes the electricity comes with such high intensity that the cables on the poles catch fire. Yesterday too, fire was burning on every pole in the entire locality.When my cousin was about to leave home in the morning, there was such a strong electric current in the gate that there was no way to save him. The current had spread throughout the entire gate. After much effort, when we broke the electricity meter with sticks and cut the wires, only then did the fire extinguish and they could be rescued. The atmosphere there was like an explosion. We complained repeatedly, my sister-in-law also gave it in writing, but the electricity department has not paid any attention to it till date. In this accident, one of my nephews and my cousin have passed away, and my aunt is admitted to the hospital in serious condition. Responsible officers did not wake up even after written complaint Pankaj Kumar, who was present at the spot, has made serious allegations against the administration. He said that the village transformer often had problems, and the electricity sometimes came very low and sometimes so high that the cables caught fire. A written complaint about this was made to the electricity department officials as well as the local MLA. But no one solved the problem. Villagers have now demanded strict action against the guilty officials and compensation for the victims.

stories.title: Mayawati calls for control on petroleum prices:People already troubled by inflation; fuel hike sparks concern
stories.summary: BSP chief Mayawati has warned the government about the simultaneous increase of Rs 993 in the price of commercial gas cylinders. She said that this increase has spread unrest among common people. Mayawati said that the prices of cooking gas, petrol, diesel, and other petroleum products may also increase soon. She appealed to the government to follow the same policy now, just as petroleum prices were kept under control during the elections. BSP chief Mayawati said, Whether it's the US-Israel war on Iran or any other reason, such a sudden large increase in prices is troubling the common public. The government should keep prices under control in public interest. She informed that in Delhi, the price of a commercial cylinder at the new rate will now exceed approximately three thousand rupees. Mayawati said that this increase will badly affect the poor and middle-class people who are already struggling with inflation. Therefore, the government should formulate policies only after reassessing its decision.

stories.title: Assam Rifles jawan’s celebratory firing kills child in Ballia:Bullet passes through 8-yr-old boy’s chest, police register case
stories.summary: An eight-year-old boy was killed after being hit during celebratory firing at a wedding in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh. The boy died on the spot after the bullet passed through his chest. Sunil Yadav, the accused, who's an Assam Rifles jawan, fled the scene after the incident in Shivpur Diar on Friday night. Meanwhile, police have registered an FIR in the case. First see 2 pictures... The case in detail On Friday, a wedding ceremony of two daughters of Prem Yadav was being held in Purwa Pandey ka Dera village. Both wedding processions had arrived from Bihar. Around 10:15 pm, during the welcome of the baraat and dance celebrations, some people began celebratory firing. During the firing, Prem Yadav’s brother-in-law Sunil Yadav also joined in and fired his double-barrel gun. During the firing, his weapon reportedly became unbalanced and a bullet struck 8-year-old Veer Yadav, son of Sanjay Yadav, who was standing nearby in the baraat. The bullet passed through the child’s chest. He collapsed on the spot and died. After the incident, panic spread in the wedding gathering. The family was thrown into chaos. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Upon receiving information, police reached the spot and sent the body for post-mortem. Based on a complaint by the family, an FIR has been registered against the accused jawan. Meanwhile, the joy of the wedding turned into mourning, and after completing formal rituals, the ceremonies were concluded and the baraat was sent back. Police team formed to arrest the accused Additional Superintendent of Police (South) Sanjay Verma said- A child has died due to celebratory firing. The person who fired the shot is a relative. An FIR has been registered based on the family’s complaint, and a police team has been formed to arrest the accused.

stories.title: UP Congress chief Ajay Rai in ICU after chest pain:PM Modi, Rahul Gandhi wish speedy recovery; his condition is now stable
stories.summary: UP Congress chief Ajay Rai’s health suddenly deteriorated on Friday afternoon. He became unconscious and was immediately admitted to Medanta Hospital. In the emergency ward, he was treated under the supervision of specialist doctors and later shifted to the ICU. His condition is now said to be out of danger. Ajay Rai complained of chest pain and fainted inside his car while returning home. Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted on ‘X’ at 11:54 pm on Friday, wishing him a speedy recovery. He wrote that he was saddened to hear about Ajay Rai’s illness and prayed for his quick recovery. Nearly 11 hours later, at 11:13 am on Saturday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also posted on X expressing concern over his health and wished him a fast recovery, hoping he returns to public service with full strength. Meanwhile, UP Congress in-charge Avinash Pande said Ajay Rai’s condition is stable and he is likely to be discharged soon. Chest pain at party office, collapsed on way home In Lucknow, the Congress party held a teachers’ and doctors’ conference on Friday on Labour Day and Buddha Purnima, attended by several leaders including Avinash Pande and Supriya Shrinate. After the programme, Ajay Rai went to drop UP in-charge Avinash Pande at the airport and later returned to the party office at Mall Avenue, where another event was underway. It was here that he developed chest pain and told colleagues he was feeling uneasy and needed to go home. While being taken to his apartment in Telibagh, his condition worsened and he fainted in the car. He was immediately rushed to Medanta Hospital. Tests conducted to rule out heart attack Medanta Lucknow director Dr Rakesh Kapoor said Ajay Rai was admitted to the emergency ward with complaints of chest pain, uneasiness and fainting. He was treated under specialist supervision. Blood samples were sent for testing. Considering the possibility of a heart attack, Troponin-T and Troponin-I tests were conducted, which came out normal. A brain CT scan was also done to rule out stroke, and no serious issue was found. Doctors confirmed that there is currently no danger to his health. stories.title: ‘Two stools don’t make a chair’:Akhilesh Yadav shares video and takes dig at UP deputy CMs; Keshav hits back, says, 'Natural to be wary of duo pair'
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday night shared a controversial reel of UP Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak on ‘X’, drawing sharp reactions from them. The video with the background music, “Duniya ke thagon se bachne zara…,” captioned “Do stools ko milane se kursi nahi banti,” takes a dig at the leaders. Fourteen hours later, Maurya hits back at Akhilesh Yadav, claiming Akhilesh’s fear of the “fit and hit pair” is justified. Replying to his post on X, Maurya wrote the atrocities committed against the deprived and labour classes under Akhilesh’s rule have neither been forgotten nor will they be forgotten. The public will settle accounts by making the lotus bloom. Akhilesh's video shows both Deputy CMs together The video, shared by Akhilesh at 10 pm, captures both Deputy CMs when they visited Kushinagar on the occasion of Buddha Purnima on Friday. Both leaders are seen walking and smiling in a park in the video with the song, “Duniya ke thagon se bachne zara" playing in the background. Pathak is heard saying that they are at the Mahaparinirvana site of Lord Buddha in Kushinagar. In the video, Pathak highlights Buddha’s message of peace and compassion Buddha Purnima, coinciding the International Labour Day. The video also contains remarks encouraging youth and references to developmental projects carried out in the state under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Keshav Maurya’s counter-attack on X On Saturday morning, Maurya wrote on X that he and Pathak are a “symbol of public trust”, and said that he's a descendant of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya and and draw inspiration from his ideals of building an undivided India. He also linked himself to Lord Gautam Buddha’s legacy of peace, equality and justice. Maurya said the people of Uttar Pradesh will never forget the injustices against backward and labour communities, such as Shakya, Kushwaha, Maurya, Saini and others, under Akhilesh Yadav’s reign. The answer to such injustices will be given democratically by making the “lotus bloom”. What expert says on their political rivalry Senior journalist and political expert Prem Kant Tripathi said Akhilesh’s “thagon” remark should be viewed in the context of his "Pichhda, Dalit and Adivasi (PDA)" politics. Tripathi said Maurya tried to connect himself with Maurya dynasty, yet, at the same time, BJP is responding to a backward leader through another backward leader, while CM Yogi himself avoids direct responses to Akhilesh's criticisms. Akhilesh-Maurya rivalry isn't new It is not the first time that both leaders traded barbs in public. Both leaders are rooted in OBC politics and have exchanged heated remarks in the Assembly before. They also disagree over who to credit for caste census. While Akhilesh claimed it was due to SP pressure, Maurya credited it to BJP. During the Maha Kumbh mela, Akhilesh raised questions on water quality of the “Sangam”, which Maurya called an insult to “Sanatan Dharma”. Akhilesh had earlier called Maurya a “Delhi’s pawn” and “Delhi Wi-Fi password,” and Maurya responded by calling SP as "Samaptwadi Party”. Attacks intensify post-Lok Sabha election After the Lok Sabha elections, Akhilesh intensified attacks on Keshav Maurya. Experts say SP’s PDA formula worked in the elections, with 37 MPs elected, out of which a large number belonged to backward communities. Since then, Akhilesh has repeatedly targeted Maurya, calling him a “Delhi pawn” and even offering slogans like “bring 100, form government,” while BJP has responded through counter-remarks.

stories.title: Kashi saints condemn Maulana Sajid Rashidi statement:Demand strict action over alleged provocative remarks; says statement dangerous for unity, peace
stories.summary: There is deep anger in the saint community of Kashi over a controversial statement made by Maulana Sajid Rashidi. The saints have described it as an attempt to disturb social harmony and have demanded strict action from the administration. The Sant Samiti general secretary Swami Jeetendranand Saraswati took a strong stand in the matter and issued a warning statement. He said that such provocative and violent statements not only increase tension in society but also pose a threat to the unity and peace of the country. Addressing Maulana Sajid Rashidi, Swami Jeetendranand Saraswati said that talking about violence against any religion or community is highly irresponsible. He also said that the Hindu community believes in law, the Constitution and the government, but this does not mean that anyone can continuously use provocative language without any response. What is the controversy? During an interview, Maulana Sajid Rashidi allegedly said that “if you do not recite the Kalma, you will be killed” and also stated that until fear is created in the Hindu community, they will not listen. After this statement came to light, the issue has been escalating. Reaction of the saint community The saints of Kashi have termed the statement highly objectionable and provocative. They said that such remarks spread enmity in society. The Sant Samiti has demanded that the administration investigate the matter and take appropriate legal action so that no one uses such language in the future.

stories.title: Kanpur doctors implant world's smallest pacemaker in 77-year-old man:Install ₹20 lakh wireless device without surgery for free
stories.summary: Doctors at the Heart Institute (Cardiology) have achieved a major breakthrough in medical treatment by giving a 77-year-old man a new lease of life with the world’s smallest wireless pacemaker — implanted without major surgery or any incision. What makes the case more remarkable is that the capsule-sized pacemaker, which costs around ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh in the market, was provided free of cost to the patient under a government health scheme. 77-year-old from Mainpuri suffered dizziness, heartbeat dropped to just 20 Hargovind, a 77-year-old resident of Mainpuri, had been frequently feeling weak and would suddenly collapse unconscious. When he was brought to the Heart Institute in Kanpur, tests revealed that he had a complete heart blockage. His heartbeat, which should normally be around 70, had dropped drastically to just 20 to 40 beats per minute. Blocked veins ruled out conventional pacemaker surgery Senior doctor Avadhesh Sharma said the patient’s condition was extremely serious. Normally, a pacemaker is implanted through surgery near the collar bone, but in Hargovind’s case, severe blockage in the veins made the traditional procedure impossible. Doctors then opted for the world’s most advanced capsule pacemaker. Why this tiny device is better than a regular pacemaker A conventional pacemaker is about the size of a matchbox and is implanted under the skin through surgery. It carries a risk of infection and its battery usually lasts only 10 to 12 years. In contrast, the capsule pacemaker has no wires, eliminating the risk of veins getting blocked in the future. Its battery life is also significantly longer — around 20 to 25 years — reducing the need for replacement. ₹20 lakh treatment provided free under Pandit Deendayal scheme The cost of the advanced treatment had initially worried the family, as the device is priced between ₹15 lakh and ₹20 lakh in the market. However, the institute carried out the entire treatment free of charge under the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Scheme. Following the successful procedure, Kanpur’s Heart Institute is now moving towards becoming a Centre of Excellence in advanced cardiac care. Capsule reached the heart through a vein in the leg Dr Umeshwar Pandey, Dr SK Sinha and their team carried out the complex procedure by inserting the tiny wireless capsule pacemaker through a vein in the patient’s leg (groin) and guiding it directly into the heart, where it was implanted. The entire process was completed without any incision or stitches.

stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has set a target of providing jobs to 1.5 lakh youths this year. Around 80,000 recruitments are likely in the Police Department, while nearly 50,000 vacancies may be filled in the Education Department. Apart from this, recruitments have also been proposed in the Revenue, Medical, Judicial, Women and Child Development departments. s for several vacancies have already been issued. The government aims to achieve its larger goal of providing 10 lakh jobs in 10 years. Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh are scheduled for February-March 2027, and the Model Code of Conduct is expected to come into force by January 2027. This means the current BJP government has only eight months left to announce recruitments, conduct examinations and declare results. Which departments are recruiting, what are the qualifications, and how will recruitment be conducted? Here’s a detailed report… 46 candidates competing for every Home Guard post Examinations for 41,424 Home Guard posts in Uttar Pradesh were held on April 25, 26 and 27. A total of 19,29,155 candidates appeared for the exam — meaning there are 46 applicants for every single post. The written examination result is likely to be declared between June 15 and June 30. Only candidates who clear the written test will be called for the physical examination. 15 lakh candidates appeared for UPSI exam Last month, on March 14 and 15, examinations were conducted for 4,543 UPSI posts. Around 15 lakh candidates appeared in the examination. Centres were set up across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh. The result is expected by May 10. Applications were accepted till January 28, while the examination is scheduled for May 21. The paper will carry 100 marks, with 100 questions. The pattern will be objective type, and 0.25 marks will be deducted for every wrong answer. Only candidates who cleared UP PET-2025 were eligible to apply. Around 3.66 lakh candidates fall in this category. What should be the age of the candidate? Recruitment for 929 posts of ASO-ARO UPSSSC has invited applications for Assistant Statistical Officer (ASO) and Assistant Research Officer (ARO) posts. Out of 929 total posts: The notification was issued on April 21. The last date to apply is May 11. The examination date has not been announced yet. What should be the age of the candidate? Recruitment for 402 posts of Assistant Boring Technician UPSSSC has announced recruitment for 402 Assistant Boring Technician posts. Applications can be submitted between April 15 and May 5. Candidates must: After the written examination, there will be document verification, followed by the joining process. What should be the age of the candidate? Now about those recruitments which are proposed Applications for Lower PCS from May 29 UPSSSC has announced recruitment for 2,285 posts, including: Applications will open from May 29. Candidates must: The examination may be held in July. Applications for Forest Guard to start from June 30 UPSSSC has announced recruitment for 708 Forest Guard posts. Applications will begin on June 30, and the last date to apply is July 20. Teacher recruitment may happen in September-October On February 17, 2026, the Education Minister informed the Assembly that 46,944 teaching posts are vacant in Uttar Pradesh. No recruitment has been conducted at the Basic Education level (Classes 1 to 8) since 2018. The government is set to conduct the TET examination on July 2, 3 and 4. s for around 35,000 posts are likely to be issued by September-October. 25,000 posts likely in Secondary Education Department Around 25,000 recruitments may also take place in the Secondary Education Department in the coming months. stories.title: Smart meter anger spills onto UP streets:Women uproot meters, dump them at power offices; Akhilesh targets govt
stories.summary: In Agra, Firozabad and several other cities, hundreds of women uprooted smart meters installed at their homes, carried them on their heads to electricity department offices and threw them there in protest. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also took a swipe at the government over the protests, saying, “The public has caught the theft.” Watch the video to see why people are angry over smart meters.

stories.title: May begins in UP with cool winds, rain:Temperatures drop, heatwave relief likely for 10 days
stories.summary: The start of May in Uttar Pradesh has brought relief, with light rain and strong winds over the past three days leading to a drop in temperatures on Friday. Cool winds throughout the day provided respite from intense heat, and the weather remained pleasant. Maximum temperatures in several districts remained well below normal. Gorakhpur recorded a maximum of 26.4°C — the third lowest in observation history — while Ballia logged 27.5°C, the fifth lowest on record. In 15 districts, maximum temperatures ranged between 30°C and 32°C. In contrast, Orai was the hottest at 41.6°C, while Hardoi recorded a minimum temperature of 17°C. See weather pictures- Good rainfall in 24 hours; fresh rain expected from May 4 Several districts recorded substantial rainfall in the past 24 hours — Kannauj (54 mm), Balrampur (52.6 mm), Lakhimpur Kheri (51.8 mm), Bareilly (29 mm), and Gorakhpur (23.8 mm). The rain helped lower temperatures and provided relief from heat. According to Dr Atul Singh, senior scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre in Lucknow, the weather is expected to remain dry for the next two days, with temperatures likely to rise by 6 to 8°C due to sunshine. A fresh western disturbance is expected to become active from May 4, which may trigger another spell of storms and rain. No heatwave expected in early May As per the monthly forecast, Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive above-normal rainfall in May 2026. However, heatwave days may be above normal in the Terai region, while eastern UP is expected to see normal conditions. Overall, maximum and minimum temperatures across most parts of the state are likely to remain normal or slightly above normal. The weather department has clarified that no heatwave conditions are expected during the first 10 days of May due to active weather systems. Rain damages crops; CM orders compensation survey Continuous rainfall has caused damage to crops, particularly vegetables. Farmers fear losses to cucumber, melon, and watermelon crops, with concerns of rotting due to excess moisture. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to assess the damage on the ground and prepare reports swiftly so that compensation can be provided to affected farmers. How will the weather be for the next 5 days? Mixed conditions ahead: warm nights, localised heat Some areas may still experience heatwave conditions during afternoons, along with warmer nights. A fresh spell of rain and thunderstorms may bring a temperature drop of 2–4°C, improving heatwave conditions. Rain activity is expected to begin in western UP and gradually move eastward. El Niño concern for monsoon Between June and September, Uttar Pradesh and the rest of the country may receive below-normal rainfall. IMD Director General Dr M Mohapatra said conditions are shifting from La Niña to El Niño in the Pacific Ocean, which typically leads to reduced rainfall. stories.title: BJP leader, businessman arrested over double murder:Alleged affair between married employee and divorced woman turns fatal
stories.summary: Two murders within 15 days in Baghpat have shocked locals, with both bodies later recovered in Saharanpur. The victims were contractual employee Vikrant and his girlfriend Rakhi. Rakhi, known for carrying a pistol, had been divorced twice and was in a relationship with 42-year-old married Vikrant. The back-to-back killings left people wondering what led to the double murder. Around 15 days after the killings, main accused BJP Yuva Morcha leader Sudharas Chauhan was arrested from Baghpat on May 1 (Friday), revealing the full sequence. Police say the double murder involved a love affair, betrayal, disputes, fear of being caught and political links. Here’s a detailed account of the case and its key characters… Vikrant was originally from Prayagraj and had been working as a contractual employee with DUDA (District Urban Development Agency) in Baghpat since 2018. On April 15, 2026, he reached office, worked as usual and returned in the evening to his rented accommodation in Arjunpuram Colony. When he did not report to office on April 16, his colleagues tried calling him, but his phone was switched off. His family was then informed. Wife filed missing complaint on April 23 Vikrant’s wife Prachi (35) works in the Irrigation and Water Resources Department in Noida. The two were married 10 years ago and have a daughter. Distressed by her husband’s disappearance, Prachi searched for him among relatives. After exhausting all options, she filed a missing complaint on April 23. She raised suspicion about a woman named Rakhi, saying Vikrant was in contact with her and that she was putting pressure on him and threatening him to fulfil her demands. Following this, police swung into action and began their investigation. Rakhi's entry in the case...who was later murdered Based on the missing complaint filed by Vikrant’s wife Prachi, police extracted Rakhi’s mobile call details. It was found that Vikrant had been in frequent contact with Rakhi Kashyap. On April 18, Baghpat police questioned Rakhi. Several questions were asked, but she kept giving evasive answers. Vikrant's body recovered on April 17 On April 17, police in Saharanpur recovered a body from a canal, but it could not be identified. The body was wrapped in cloth, hands and legs were tied, and heavy blows had been inflicted on the head and face to make identification difficult. While Saharanpur and Baghpat police were investigating this unidentified body, another body — of an unidentified woman — was recovered on April 27 from the forests of Naugaon under Mirzapur police station limits. She had been murdered with a sharp weapon and her throat had also been slit. Later, she was identified as Rakhi. After that, the entire case began unfolding layer by layer. Shot fired at party hit Vikrant...body thrown in canal Two arrests have been made in the case so far. Investigation has revealed that on April 16, a party was held at Rakhi’s house in Baghpat. Present at the gathering were Vikrant, Rakhi, Rakhi’s friend and former BJP Yuva Morcha city president Sudharas Chauhan, medicine trader Kapil Chauhan and others. The party was hosted by Sudharas Chauhan. During the gathering, an argument broke out over some issue. The dispute escalated so much that Rakhi allegedly shot Vikrant in the thigh with her licensed pistol. The three panicked. Instead of taking injured Vikrant to hospital, they took him to a deserted place, tied his hands and legs, wrapped him in cloth and dumped him. Later, Rakhi’s body was also found. Her throat had been slit, and she had multiple knife wounds on her chest and back. In Rakhi’s murder case, police have detained Sudharas Chauhan and Kapil Chauhan and questioned them, but police have not yet made an official disclosure. Now read...about Rakhi who lived a luxury life? Police investigation revealed that 27-year-old Rakhi Kashyap was a resident of Rajpur-Khampur village in Baghpat. Her life — marked by a luxury lifestyle, a licensed pistol in hand and expensive tastes — looked glamorous from the outside, but was deeply complicated within. Two marriages — the first in Meerut, the second elsewhere — both ended in divorce. She had no contact with her family for seven years. Living in different places and creating a new identity each time had become part of her life. Rakhi’s father Sherdeen died four years ago. Her elder brother Rajeev runs a chowmein cart, while her younger brother is Vikas. After her divorce, Rakhi first lived in Khekra and later shifted to Arjunpuram Colony in Baghpat. She rented a room there by introducing herself as a contractual worker in DUDA. According to locals and the police probe, Rakhi had disputes with several people and was accused of cheating many. She allegedly trapped people in romantic relationships and extorted money from them. She was also in contact with several influential people, including some political leaders. Her social media account had around 11,000 followers and she had made 1,903 posts. There were posts from Thailand on Instagram. She also made reels while carrying her licensed pistol tucked at her waist. Other posts on her account also mentioned trips to several countries. Rakhi-Vikrant were in a relationship for three years Police investigation revealed that Vikrant and Rakhi had been in a relationship for around three years. Records showed regular phone calls and long conversations between them. The two were even planning to get married. ₹4 lakh withdrawn from account two days earlier Two days before going missing, Vikrant withdrew ₹4 lakh from his bank account. It is being said that in December 2025, Vikrant and Rakhi had a serious dispute over some matter. In anger, Rakhi allegedly set Vikrant’s car on fire. Now know why Rakhi was murdered? According to police, Sudharas Chauhan and Kapil Chauhan — accused in Vikrant’s murder — feared they would be exposed. Rakhi was a crucial link in the entire episode and knew too much. That is why they allegedly planned to eliminate her too. Rakhi was called to a farmhouse, where she was kept back on the pretext of a party. There, she was murdered by slitting her throat with a knife. After that, her body was packed in a sack and thrown into the canal embankment. Mobile location data from nearby areas helped police reach the suspects. According to the postmortem report, the accused first slit Rakhi’s throat, then stabbed her multiple times in the chest and back. On Friday, Rakhi’s younger brother Vikas reached Saharanpur. He refused to take the body back to Baghpat. After police counselled him, Vikas performed Rakhi’s last rites in Saharanpur itself, in the presence of police.

stories.title: BJP still strong in UP but needs candidate overhaul:Voters upset with MLAs; SP may gain more seats
stories.summary: With barely eight months left for the enforcement of the model code of conduct ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, political parties have ramped up preparations. A large-scale ground survey indicates that while the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) remains the preferred choice among voters in the state, it faces a significant challenge—public dissatisfaction with many of its sitting MLAs and ministers. SP appears to gaining ground The findings suggest that for the BJP to retain power in the 2027 Assembly elections, it may need to replace several incumbent legislators. At the same time, the Samajwadi Party (SP) appears to be gaining ground, with its projected seat tally rising. Meanwhile, BJP’s allies are witnessing erosion in their support base, a shift that may ultimately benefit the BJP itself. Widespread public discontent against MLAs The survey highlights deep public resentment toward elected representatives across party lines. Out of BJP’s 257 MLAs, voters expressed dissatisfaction with 222. The primary reasons cited were lack of development work, poor accessibility, and unsatisfactory behavior. Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi noted that many MLAs have failed to connect with the public. According to him, representatives who remained distant—often not stepping out of their comfort zones to engage with constituents—naturally invited criticism. He added that over the past four years, even the opposition has failed to mount significant public-interest movements, leaving citizens to struggle with routine issues at local administrative levels such as tehsils, police stations, and block offices. The trend is not limited to the ruling party. Among SP’s 105 MLAs, 91 also faced public dissatisfaction, indicating a broader systemic issue in political representation. Replacing candidates has historically benefited BJP The survey underscores a crucial electoral pattern: changing candidates has previously worked in BJP’s favor. In the 2022 Assembly elections, BJP and its ally Apna Dal (S) dropped 104 out of their 318 sitting MLAs—approximately 32%—due to anti-incumbency sentiments. Of the new candidates fielded, 80 went on to win, validating the strategy. In contrast, during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, BJP largely retained its sitting MPs despite local-level dissatisfaction. The result was a sharp decline in seats—from 62 to 33 in Uttar Pradesh—highlighting the risks of ignoring voter sentiment. Hindutva and Development still drive BJP’s popularity Despite dissatisfaction with individual representatives, the BJP continues to enjoy strong support as a party. The survey found that even though around 88% of MLAs from both ruling and opposition parties faced criticism, voters still preferred the BJP overall. Senior journalist Sunita Aron explained that elections have increasingly become leader-centric. In Uttar Pradesh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath remains a dominant figure for the BJP, while Akhilesh Yadav leads the SP. As voters focus more on leadership and party identity rather than individual candidates, legislators have become less accountable for development work. She added that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s image—centered on Hindutva and development—continues to resonate with voters, keeping the BJP ahead despite local grievances. SP gains seats but faces challenges in Western UP The survey suggests that the Samajwadi Party is improving its position, with its seat count projected to rise from 105 to around 135. The gains are primarily seen in regions such as Purvanchal, Awadh, Braj, and Kanpur-Bundelkhand. However, SP faces setbacks in western Uttar Pradesh, where it needs to recalibrate its social and political equations. The region has a complex demographic mix, including Jats, Muslims, Gurjars, and Dalits. Apart from Muslims, SP lacks a strong independent vote base here. Previously, SP benefited from its alliance with the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), which has since ended. The party is now attempting to rebuild its support among Jats and Gurjars. Sunita Aron pointed out that polarization remains a significant factor in western UP, particularly in Muslim-majority districts. Additionally, parties led by Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad are also influencing voter dynamics in the region. BJP’s recent developmental push in western UP has further strengthened its position. Allies losing ground, BJP gains indirect advantage Another key takeaway from the survey is the declining influence of BJP’s allies, including Apna Dal (S), Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), Nishad Party, and RLD. These parties, often centered around caste-based politics, appear to be losing their support base. Out of 33 MLAs from these allied parties, only three received positive feedback from voters, while 30 faced dissatisfaction. However, these allies remained the top choice in only eight constituencies. This decline could indirectly benefit the BJP. In regions like Purvanchal, where allies like Nishad Party, SBSP, and Apna Dal (S) have traditionally held sway, their weakening support base appears to be shifting toward the BJP. Sunita Aron observed that voters are increasingly consolidating around national or major regional parties, moving away from smaller caste-based outfits. Harshvardhan Tripathi added that allies often engage in pressure politics while being part of the government, which can undermine their credibility among voters. Ministers face greater scrutiny and Higher expectations The survey also highlights dissatisfaction with ministers, which is even more pronounced than with MLAs. When an MLA becomes a minister, public expectations from that constituency rise significantly, with hopes of accelerated development. Tripathi explained that the BJP has been in power in Uttar Pradesh for nearly nine years, and several leaders have held ministerial positions for extended periods. Over time, expectations from both the public and party workers increase. While broader themes like Hindutva and development may resonate at the macro level, neglect of local issues and poor responsiveness to party workers’ concerns can fuel resentment. If ministers are perceived as unapproachable or indifferent, dissatisfaction intensifies further. He warned that a lack of coordination between the government, party organization, and grassroots workers could create challenges for the BJP in the upcoming elections if not addressed in time. Caste remains a factor, but not the only one Interestingly, the survey found that voters did not explicitly cite caste as a primary factor in their preferences. Among various reasons for liking or disliking candidates, caste was the least mentioned. This suggests a shift in voter behaviour. While caste dynamics continue to influence politics in Uttar Pradesh, voters appear to be increasingly considering factors such as performance, accessibility, and leadership. If caste alone were decisive, BJP’s allies—many of whom rely heavily on caste-based support—would not be witnessing a decline. The findings indicate that no party can rely solely on caste equations to secure an electoral victory in the state.

stories.title: 7 trapped as water tank collapses in Bareilly:Victims were playing cards underneath; structure was built 4 years ago under Jal Jeevan Mission
stories.summary: In Bareilly on Monday, 7 people were trapped after a water tank of the Jal Jeevan Mission collapsed. All of them were sitting near the tank playing cards. As soon as the tank fell, there was a very loud explosion-like sound. Hearing this, the villagers rushed to the spot. When they saw, the entire tank had collapsed. The villagers immediately removed the debris and pulled out the trapped people. They were immediately rushed to the hospital for treatment. One of the injured is said to be in serious condition. Upon receiving information about the accident, police administration and SDRF teams reached the spot. They started removing the debris. The incident occurred in the Bhamora area at 5 PM. See 2 pictures of the rescue Tank was built at a cost of over 3 crore Jal Nigam had built a tank four years ago in Sardar Nagar Gram Panchayat of Bhamora development block, Alampur Jafrabad. On Monday evening around 5 PM, the tank suddenly collapsed. As a result, 7 people playing cards near the tank were buried under the debris. Upon receiving the information, officials reached the spot, and the police sent all the injured to the hospital. The injured include Dori Lal, Veerpal, Arjun, Ravindra alias Dabbu, and Bedpal. Villagers Avnesh Kumar, Naresh Sharma, Sanjeev Pathak, Sachin Chauhan, and others stated that the government had constructed the water tank in 2022 under the Jal Jeevan Mission at a cost of three crore sixty-two lakh eighty-seven thousand rupees. Water had reached homes 8 months ago Pradhan's husband Sartaj Mansoori said that contractor Amrish had carried out the construction under the supervision of Jal Nigam's JE Nityanand. After the construction of the tank, water supply through taps to every household had started for the villagers eight months ago. Upon receiving the information, CO Nitin Kumar, who arrived with the police, sent all the injured to private and government hospitals. SDM Aonla Bidushi Singh reached the spot along with ADM E. The administration team is removing the debris of the tank.

stories.title: UP staff transfers scheduled between 5 and 31 May:New policy gets approval, summons will come via WhatsApp
stories.summary: Transfers of 1.6 million employees and officers in UP will be done from May 5 to May 31. The Yogi cabinet approved the transfer policy for 2026-27 on Monday. Officers and employees who have completed three years of service in a district and seven years in a division will be subject to transfer. Couples in government service will be posted at the same location. Relief will be provided to disabled employees and those suffering from serious illnesses. 29 proposals have been approved in the cabinet. Parliamentary Affairs and Finance Minister Suresh Khanna stated at the Lok Bhawan Media Center that 20 percent of employees and officers will be transferred compared to the total sanctioned posts in departments. Know the important decisions Now e-summons will be issued To expedite the disposal of pending cases in the state's courts, the state government has now implemented the e-summons system. Cases used to take time for disposal due to summons issued by the court not being served on time, or due to the concerned complainant, plaintiff, or witness not accepting personal summons. In the cabinet meeting, the Uttar Pradesh E-Evidence Management Rules, Uttar Pradesh Electronic Summons Issuance and Service Rules 2026, and Community Service Guidelines 2026 have been approved. Under this, summons can now be issued via email and WhatsApp, and these will be considered authorized. Farmers will get compensation for towers and power lines Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma said that in the state, 765, 490, 220, and 132 KV high-tension lines are laid through farmers' fields. Large electricity towers are also installed. Before 2018, there was no provision for compensation for power lines and towers passing through fields. However, this provision was made in 2018, but farmers were not satisfied due to the very low compensation amount in that provision. Because of this, there were difficulties in laying power lines and installing towers in the fields. The government has now made a provision to increase the compensation amount. For the land located within a one-meter radius of the spot where an electricity tower will be installed in the field, the farmer will be given double the compensation based on the circle rate. For laying electricity lines across the field, up to 30 percent of the land's value will be given as compensation. Solar Plant to be Installed in Jalaun The Energy Minister stated that the use of renewable energy is increasing in the state. To reduce global warming and promote green energy, a 500 MW capacity solar plant will be installed in Jalaun. For its installation, in this plant being set up under the joint auspices of Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Generation Corporation and Coal India Limited, 45 percent share will belong to the state government and 56 percent to Coal India Limited. Power Stations to be established in YEIDA The Energy Minister stated that new industries are being established in the Yamuna Expressway Authority area in Noida. To improve the electricity supply system there, three new 400/220 KVA power stations will be built. It will cost 653 crore rupees. Industries coming up in the Greater Noida and Yamuna Authority areas will benefit from this. One District One Dish Scheme Approved MSME Minister Rakesh Sachan informed that the Cabinet has approved the One District-One Dish scheme. The scheme will give national and international recognition to one dish from each district. A unique dish from the district will be selected for the scheme. Efforts will be made to improve their packaging and quality. Along with developing a logo for the dish, it will be branded. By training relevant traders and artisans, the dishes will be made available in various festivals and events. Along with increasing their production, a market will also be provided. He said, UP holds a distinct identity in traditional cuisine. Agra's Petha, Mathura's Peda, Gorakhpur's Litti Chokha, Meerut's Gajak, Jaunpur's Imarti, Farrukhabad's Dalmoth - all these dishes have been the identity of these districts for centuries. Efforts will be made to increase income by giving them a distinct identity at national and international levels. He informed that a division-wise list has been prepared. To effectively implement the scheme, a vendor conference will be organized at Rashtra Prerna Sthal in Lucknow. A conference of food vendors and confectioners will be held, and universities and technical institutions working in the food sector will be included in this conference. Information on technology and packaging in the food sector will be provided, and excellent dishes will be showcased by setting up stalls. Under the scheme, investors will be given up to 25 percent subsidy. Textile parks will be established Rakesh Sachan informed that the state government had set a target to establish 10 textile parks in the state under the Sant Kabir Textile and Apparel Park scheme. Currently, the work of establishing a textile park is underway in Varanasi, and 75 acres of land have been acquired. In the cabinet meeting held on Monday, textile parks will be established on the land of spinning mills: 79 acres in Amroha, 79 acres in Baheri of Bareilly, 40 acres in Sant Kabir Nagar, and 52 acres in Nagina of Bijnor. Investors have been invited through master developers, and these parks will provide employment to millions of people, creating jobs in the textile sector in UP. A private university will be established in Firozabad Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay said, the Cabinet has approved issuing a letter of intent to Amardeep Memorial Trust for the establishment of Amardeep University Firozabad, under the Uttar Pradesh Private Universities Act. The proposal to grant a letter of authority for the operation of Metro University in Noida has also been approved. 35 crore saplings will be planted Minister of State for Forest and Environment, Arun Saxena, informed that 35 crore saplings will be planted in the financial year 2026-27 to increase green cover and tree plantation. A demand of Rs 147 crore has been made for tree plantation in departments, undertakings, railways, defense, industrial units, private and government institutions of the state government and the Government of India. Saplings will be planted with public participation. 30 percent fruit-bearing trees will be planted. 150 CM Fellows to be recruited Alok Kumar, Principal Secretary of the Industrial Development Department, informed that an OTD cell was constituted under the chairmanship of the District Magistrate to make the state's economy a one trillion dollar economy. To assist this cell, two OTD CM Fellows will be deployed in each district. One should be proficient in the field of economic development and the other OTD Fellow will provide services related to data analysis. The age limit for CM Fellows has been set at 40 years, while a monthly honorarium of 50 thousand rupees will be given. A housing allowance of ten thousand rupees will be provided. A laptop worth 40 thousand rupees will be given. CM Fellows will be recruited for three years, after which their tenure can be extended by one year at a time. CM Fellows who have served for three years will get age relaxation in recruitment examinations conducted by various recruitment commissions of the state government. Finance Minister Suresh Khanna informed that for the smooth and efficient functioning of the judicial work of the High Court Lucknow Bench, the tenure of 145 Law Clerks will be extended from two years to three years. A monthly honorarium of 40 thousand rupees is given. Finance Minister Suresh Khanna said that just as Tata has taken 150 ITIs, similarly, to impart technical knowledge to children, Dream Skill Labs will be established in 150 government schools in collaboration with Nelco Network Products Ltd. In the first phase, labs will be established at every divisional headquarters in the state. 68 percent of the money will be from Tata Nelco, and 32 percent will be from the state government. On this, Tata Nelco will spend 1360 crore rupees and the department will spend 640.20 crore rupees. In the first phase, one Dream Skill Lab will be established at each divisional headquarters.

stories.title: Yogi’s Bengal campaign sees BJP leading in 31 seats:CM achieves 89% strike rate, Rajnath at 83% and Keshav at 78%
stories.summary: In the West Bengal Assembly elections, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath campaigned on the highest number of seats among leaders from the state, covering 35 constituencies. According to Election Commission data on results and trends available till 8 pm, BJP candidates have either won or are leading on 31 of these seats, which is about 89%. The Chief Minister also campaigned on two seats in Assam. On these, one has been won by the BJP and the other by its ally Asom Gana Parishad. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh campaigned on six seats, of which BJP candidates are leading or have won on five seats, around 83%. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya’s campaign seats have also shown strong performance, with BJP candidates leading on about 78% of them. CM Yogi cornered TMC on 5 issues 1. Harassment of BJP workers CM Yogi launched a sharp attack on the plight of Bengal, saying that there was widespread chaos under Trinamool rule. The homes of BJP workers like Swarup Ghosh, Palash Ghosh, and Utpal Das were destroyed. He targeted the vote-bank traders who are changing Bengal's demography and questioned Mamata Didi's silence on the killing of Dalit Hindus in Bangladesh. 2. Cut money with the help of sand, land, and cattle mafia CM Yogi raised the issue of sand, coal, land, and cattle mafia in the Trinamool Congress government. He said that they are sucking Bengal dry. In 15 years, TMC has turned Bengal into a hub of terror, mafia rule, cut money, and corruption. 3. West Bengal's Demography is Changing CM Yogi kept asking the public in all his rallies that Bengal's identity is not from the Kaaba, but from Maa Kalibari. Then, taking a dig at Mamata Banerjee and her nephew Abhishek Banerjee, he said that the aunt-nephew duo wants to erase Bengal's existence. 4. UP Model vs. Bengal's Plight CM Yogi reiterated in every rally that before 2017, the condition of UP was similar to that of Bengal. He would say in his speech, "Earlier, riots used to happen during festivals in UP, curfews were imposed. When the double engine government was formed in 2017, everything changed. Now no curfew, no riots. Bulldozers sent goons and mafias to hell. UP has now become the growth engine of the country's economy." 5. Mention of Bengal's glorious history In rallies, the CM would remind people of Bengal's golden past, saying that Bengal gave spirituality, culture, art, and education to the country. At one time, Bengal was the backbone of India's GDP. Congress, the Left, and then TMC made it poor. Referring to the 1905 partition of Bengal protest and the Swadeshi movement, he appealed to Bengalis to unite again. He also mentioned settling 331 Hindu families from Bangladesh in Lakhimpur Kheri. Results of seats where Yogi held rallies and roadshows How CM Yogi's visit is decided According to people associated with the BJP state organization, the CM's visit is decided based on the guidelines of the National Election Management Committee. For this, the BJP's state unit and the party headquarters in Delhi play a key role. The demand for Yogi's visit is first made by the BJP's state units. The states send their demand to the Delhi party headquarters. From here, the visits are finalized. Along with this, the Election Management Committee also decides the visits of star campaigners after considering the seat situation, equations, and issues in the states. This information must be given to the state unit and the CM three to four days in advance. Sometimes, visits are also fixed suddenly. BJP in North 24 Parganas, under the charge of Suresh Rana Former UP Cabinet Minister Suresh Rana was made in-charge of North 24 Parganas. Out of 33 assembly constituencies here, BJP candidates are leading in 14, while TMC candidates are leading in 17. Additionally, several current and former UP MLAs were assigned responsibility for 47 assembly constituencies. Out of these, BJP is leading in 30. Among these prominent leaders are Dayashankar Mishra Dayalu, Minister of State Dinesh Khatik, Sanjay Gangwar, former MP Ajay Mishra Teni, Subrat Pathak, Swati Singh, Upendra Tiwari, Anand Shukla, MLC Dharmendra Bhardwaj, and Arun Pathak. BJP leads in 2 seats campaigned by Ravi Kishan BJP leading on 30 seats in Medinipur, under JPS Rathore's charge JPS Rathore, Cooperation Minister in the UP government, was given charge of Medinipur in West Bengal. BJP candidates are leading on 30 out of 35 seats here. He has also been in charge of the West Bengal Assembly election management branch in 2021. He has handled similar responsibilities in the UP elections of 2017 and 2022. BJP leading on 2 seats campaigned by Brajesh Pathak Yogi campaigned in 31 seats in Bihar, BJP won 27 Six months ago, in the Bihar elections, UP CM Yogi Adityanath held 31 public meetings and rallies. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav campaigned in 22 seats in Bihar in favor of the Grand Alliance without contesting any seat. The UP CM had a significant impact on the results. His win strike rate was over 87 percent. 27 out of 31 NDA candidates registered a win. Whereas Akhilesh Yadav's strike rate was merely 9 percent. The Grand Alliance won only two seats where he campaigned.
